items.titel: Agricultural Technology, Functional Scale and Localized Value Creation: Pathways to Structural Transformation in Bihar, India
items.samenvatting_bron: Agricultural transformation in developing agrarian economies depends not only on technological progress and increased productive capacity, but also on the capacity to deploy technological gains at economically viable scale and connect them with downstream value-adding activities. This study examines the role of functional scale in linking agricultural technological development with localized value-creation potential and broader structural transformation in Bihar, India. It develops a state-level analytical framework in which agricultural technology contributes to productive capacity and marketable output, while organizational and institutional arrangements influence the capacity to translate dispersed production into aggregation, processing, agrifood services, and wider economic transformation. Drawing on official state-level economic and agricultural statistics, the study finds that Bihar has a substantial and increasingly intensified agricultural production base. Cropping intensity increased from 147% in 2023–24 to 152% in 2024–25, while cereal production rose from 227.17 to 243.91 lakh tonnes. Indicators of functional-scale capacity also expanded: registered Farmer Producer Organizations increased from 221 in 2021 to 580 in 2024, and cumulative Custom Hiring Centres increased from 397 by 2019–20 to 832 by 2025. items.titel: With whom you elaborate matters: how learning orientation impacts cross-culture and same-culture information elaboration in culturally diverse teams
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Work teams are increasingly characterized by diverse cultural backgrounds. Although research has established that cultural diversity holds the potential to enhance team performance through information elaboration—the exchange, discussion, and integration of task-relevant information—prior work has treated elaboration as an undifferentiated process, leaving unspecified whether it occurs across or within cultural boundaries. We develop a differentiated elaboration perspective that distinguishes cross-culture information elaboration between culturally dissimilar members from same-culture information elaboration between culturally similar members. Using a multi-source, multi-wave study of 104 culturally diverse teams comprising 587 members, we found that, as expected, cross-culture elaboration was more strongly related to team performance than same-culture elaboration. Moreover, team learning orientation predicted both forms of elaboration, and its indirect association with team performance was stronger through cross-culture elaboration. These findings advance a differentiated elaboration perspective to demonstrate that elaboration that crosses cultural boundaries is more important for diverse teams than same-culture elaboration. This points to opportunities for future research on reaping the benefits of diverse teams.

items.titel: Living Without Work: A Phenomenological Study of the Causes, Socioeconomic Effects, and Coping Mechanisms of Unemployed and Informal Workers of a Local Community
items.samenvatting_bron: The study sought to uncover the lived experiences of unemployed and informal workers in Barangay Capitan Bayong, Impasug-ong, Bukidnon, Philippines characterized by limited employment opportunities and livelihoods that depend on the seasons. The study employed a qualitative phenomenological approach; 15 unemployed residents were purposefully selected, and in-depth interviews were conducted with them. Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis was used for analyzing data. Results indicated that factors affecting unemployment are complex and mutually reinforcing, including low education, skills mismatches, seasonal employment, job-seeking limitations due to financial difficulties, and limitations due to health status. Participants described that unemployment is not only about not earning a living, but also negatively impacting food security, children’s education, emotional health, family relations, and social involvement. In addition to the difficulties associated with unemployment, there were observations of social stigma, social exclusion, a loss of social trust, and household difficulties due to tensions. items.titel: Conditional belonging under institutional ambiguity: narratives of Sudanese asylum seekers in Eilat, Israel
items.samenvatting_bron: Introduction This qualitative study explores how Sudanese asylum seekers living in Eilat, Israel, narrate belonging under conditions of prolonged legal and institutional ambiguity. Methods Based on semi-structured in-depth interviews with 30 participants, the study examines everyday experiences across employment, education, welfare and health services, and housing, while remaining open to emergent themes, including the role of the Sudanese community. The analysis combines a multidimensional integration framework with intergroup contact theory to assess how participation in key domains interacts with status relations and institutional support. Results The analysis identified five interrelated themes: traumatic rupture and forced displacement; institutional rejection upon arrival; Eilat as a space of partial reconstruction; conditional belonging; and the dual protective and constraining role of the Sudanese community. Across employment, housing, education, and welfare and health, participants described functional integration and everyday stabilisation without corresponding legal security or broader social inclusion. Contact with members of the host society was described as largely instrumental, whereas co-ethnic networks provided essential material and emotional support in a context where opportunities for bridging ties remained limited. items.titel: Bridging global standards and local needs: a realist perspective on glocalisation in medical education
items.samenvatting_bron: Contemporary interest in glocalisation partly reflects the limitations of earlier globalising movements in medical education. The former evolves to a process through which globally-informed educational models are negotiated and reconstituted within local contexts. While global standards can enhance graduate mobility, implementation may privilege Western assumptions regarding competence, professionalism, and quality. This can lead to obscuration of local values, needs and realities. Existing scholarship has examined glocalisation through sociocultural and postcolonial perspectives, generating insights into issues of hierarchy, power, and culture. Less explored is how methodology can empower transferable explanations of how global educational interventions generate different outcomes across contexts. We argue glocalisation can be considered a wicked problem: a complex, context-dependent phenomenon shaped by interacting pedagogical, regulatory, and socio-political forces. Methodological approaches capable of leaning into such complexity have potential in expanding knowledge regarding not only whether educational interventions succeed, but how, for whom, and under what conditions. items.titel: Contextual Mission through Local Wisdom: A Lampung-Based Christian Religious Education Learning Model Integrating Missio Dei and Piil Pesenggiri
items.samenvatting_bron: Christian Religious Education in Indonesian formal schools remains largely cognitive and theoretical and seldom engages students' sociocultural realities. As a result, many students reduce Christian mission to verbal evangelism and overlook its holistic social dimensions. This study aims to construct a conceptual Christian Religious Education learning model grounded in the local wisdom of Lampung to foster students' understanding of contextual mission. The study employed a qualitative design using library research. Data were drawn from Christian Religious Education curriculum documents, mission theology literature, and scholarly works on the Lampung philosophy of Piil Pesenggiri, and were examined through qualitative content analysis involving data reduction, thematic coding, and theoretical synthesis. The findings show that the theological concept of Missio Dei and the values of Piil Pesenggiri, particularly Nemui Nyimah (hospitality) and Sakai Sambayan (mutual cooperation), share a common orientation toward hospitality, solidarity, and service, which allows them to be integrated into a single pedagogical framework. The resulting model comprises three operational phases: concept contextualization, value internalization through sociocultural moral dilemma cases, and missionary action through community-based social projects. items.titel: Effect of mobile phone-based education on HIV self-testing knowledge and uptake among female sex workers in Nigeria
items.samenvatting_bron: Female sex workers (FSWs) remain disproportionately affected by HIV infection, yet HIV testing uptake continues to be constrained by stigma, limited access to healthcare services, and inadequate knowledge of HIV prevention and self-testing approaches.= Mobile phone-based education (MPBE) represents a promising strategy for delivering accessible, confidential, and context-specific HIV prevention information to underserved populations. This study evaluated the effect of a mobile phone-based educational intervention on HIV knowledge, HIV self-testing (HIVST) knowledge, and HIVST uptake among FSWs in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, Nigeria. A two-arm quasi-experimental study was conducted among FSWs between November 2022 and March 2023. A total of 282 participants completed the study, comprising 137 participants in the intervention group and 145 in the control group. Baseline and endline assessments evaluated socio-demographic characteristics, HIV knowledge, HIVST knowledge, and HIVST uptake. The intervention group received structured HIV and HIVST education delivered through a WhatsApp-based mobile platform over five weeks, while the control group received routine HIV prevention services. items.titel: Is China’s GDP undervalued? A digital economy model
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Transactions in a digital economy generate data that firms accumulate but national accounts do not price. Within the model developed here, that omission implies measured GDP understates output. We adapt the recursive data-economy framework of Farboodi and Veldkamp (2026) to China and construct a bottom-up measure of digital investment from the itemized asset disclosures of 5,120 listed firms. The model does not identify a unique asset perimeter, so we carry two measurement boundaries throughout rather than designating one as the headline. For 2024 the adjustment is 1.60% of GDP, or 2.16 trillion RMB, under a broad boundary that includes telecommunications network assets, and 0.60%, or 0.82 trillion RMB, under a narrow boundary that excludes them. These are alternative measurement boundaries, not statistical bounds. On listed firms alone, before any extrapolation to unlisted firms, the broad-boundary figure is 0.91%. Because the knowledge stock is not identified without forecast-error data, the broad-boundary figure carries a calibrated scenario range of 0.77–4.07%, which reflects alternative calibrations rather than sampling uncertainty. Every figure is conditional on a normalization of the mapping between measured digital investment and the value of data. A validation audit of the classifier uncovers measurement defects that are not specific to China.

items.titel: A critical analysis of English language policies in Mongolia
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract This article systematically and critically examines three English language policies enacted in Mongolia from 2001 to 2025. Using critical discourse analysis (CDA) as an overarching analytical framework, the study analyzes the policy texts to identify and unpack the priorities established in these policies, the problems represented through these priorities, and the ideological orientations that shaped their construction. We employed an integrated multilevel multimethod approach (IMMA) that brings together three interdisciplinary methodological approaches: thematic coding grounded in qualitative content analysis, the What the Problem Represented to be (WPR; Bacchi, 2012) from critical policy analysis, and Discourse-Historical Approach (DHA; Reisigl & Wodak, 2009; Wodak, 2001) in critical discourse studies. Our analysis situates the policies within their social and historical context, traces their historical progression, examines the discursive practices and patterns that reflect the underlying contextual dynamics that shape the policy construction. First, we use qualitative coding to identify central themes that reflect key priorities. We then use the WPR approach to uncover the problems that are represented through these priorities and the DHA to unpack the underlying ideological orientations and social forces that shape the policy discourses. items.titel: Assessing what counts: findings from a grade 1 mathematics national diagnostic assessment in Lebanese public schools
items.samenvatting_bron: Introduction This study examines performance in Lebanon's 2025 National Diagnostic Assessment (NDA) in Grade 1 mathematics, administered by the Ministry of Education and Higher Education (MEHE) across public schools. Methods Data from 18,418 students across 818 public schools were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, supplemented by school-clustered mixed-effects models to account for the nested structure of the data. Results The overall mean score was 15.62 out of 29 (53.9%), below the MEHE 60% threshold. Although statistically significant gender and governorate differences were observed, their effect sizes were generally small, while school-level ICCs indicated substantial between-school variation (21.1%-31.9%) in continuous achievement outcomes. items.titel: Understanding the Evolution of Fintech and Sustainable Development: A Comprehensive Review
items.samenvatting_bron: This article examines the evolution of research at the intersection of financial technology (fintech) and sustainable development through a bibliometric and integrative review of 256 documents indexed in Scopus and Web of Science up to July 2024. The study illustrates the publication trends, influential sources, authors, countries, collaboration patterns, and thematic structures, and sheds light on the evolving knowledge base from a Dynamic Capabilities Theory perspective. The results reveal a significant increase in research starting from 2020, characterised by the emergence of key themes such as financial inclusion, green finance, natural resources, Sustainable Development Goals, and digital financial ecosystems. Thematic and co-occurrence analysis also shows that, across the sample, sustainable finance, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices, blockchain, big-data analytics and artificial intelligence are increasingly converging with fintech. The review suggests that fintech is not just a financial technology, but a mechanism that enables organisations and financial systems to ‘feel’ opportunities and change regarding sustainability and then capture and digitise them with financial technology, as well as reconfigure financial processes, stakeholder relationships, governance and resources. items.titel: Territorial governance for transformative change? Insights from the Chico Mendes Extractive Reserve in the Brazilian Amazon
items.samenvatting_bron: Brazilian extractive reserves constitute a model for the territorial governance of protected areas. With a focus on the territorial rights of traditional populations, they can serve as a catalyst for transformative change that reconciles the conservation of nature with the sustainable use of natural resources. However, the sustainability of land use in the Chico Mendes Extractive Reserve (CMER) is increasingly under pressure. Located in the western Amazon, sustainable forest extractivism has traditionally constituted the main livelihood of inhabitants. items.titel: Before Qualia, Strategic Existence Begins
items.samenvatting_bron: Before evolution can select anything, a physically possible causal architecture must already exist for selection to exploit. The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear. Each concept is paired with a specific biological mechanism, virion stability, irreversible adsorption, superinfection exclusion, among others, showing that the mapping is grounded in observable structure. These mappings do not reify nonhuman organisms or attribute human qualities to mindless machines. They are structural descriptions: the concepts name functions that the architecture performs, not feelings that the organism experiences. This reframes a persistent gap in philosophy of mind: qualia have long been debated while the physical architecture that must bound it has been neglected. The paper argues that power and dignity are surface forms of a deeper current—the pursuit of a pathway to existence—and that this survival architecture appears even where no mind exists to experience it. It also demonstrates improved performance in simulating summer O3 peaks, reducing maximum biases by more than 20 μg m-3, primarily through enhanced heterogeneous HONO formation and nitrate photolysis pathways that elevate OH concentrations, and it incorporates the CB6r5 mechanism to better represent biogenic VOC oxidation. The model exhibits the highest hit rate (45.6 %) for forecasting moderate PM2.5 and moderate O3 pollution events and successfully reproduces persistent pollution episodes. items.titel: Architecting Anode Current Collectors for Practical Anode-Free Alkali Metal Batteries
items.samenvatting_bron: Anode-free alkali metal batteries (AFAMBs) are emerging as a compelling strategy to surpass the cell-level energy density limits of Li-ion batteries while simplifying battery configuration. In these systems, the working anode forms in situ on a bare current collector and is continuously reshaped during cycling with a limited alkali metal inventory. As a result, the anode current collector is not merely a passive electron conductor, but a multifunctional interfacial platform that governs alkali metal nucleation, growth, stripping, and interphase evolution. This review examines the fundamental differences among anode-free lithium, sodium, and potassium systems and highlights key performance metrics for practical AFAMBs. Recent current collector engineering strategies developed for these chemistries are then summarized. Essential parameters shaping current collector design are identified, including electronic conductivity, alkali metal affinity, collector morphology, and interphase stability. Finally, practical design principles are presented to balance electrochemical performance with manufacturability under realistic operating conditions. This review aims to clarify the alkali metal-dependent design logic of current collectors and to provide guidance for the practical development of next-generation anode-free batteries.

items.titel: Molecular typing and genetic diversity of multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from Erbil City, Kurdistan Region, Iraq
items.samenvatting_bron: Background and objective: Klebsiella pneumoniae, a Gram-negative encapsulated bacterium, is one of the most significant etiological agents of healthcare- or community-acquired infections worldwide. This study set out to explore the phylogenetic relationships and genetic diversity of multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae using 16S rRNA sequencing and Multilocus Sequence Typing (MLST). Methods: A total of 298 urine samples were analyzed from patients with symptoms of urinary tract infection. Standard biochemical tests were used for isolate identification. Resistant isolates were further analyzed by molecular diagnosis through 16S rRNA gene sequencing and Multilocus Sequence Typing (MLST), in accordance with international standards. Results: Out of 298 urine specimens, 49 K. pneumoniae isolates were confirmed (isolation rate: 16.4%). Resistance was high: 49% to amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, 38.8% to cefazolin, 34.7% to ceftriaxone, and 12.2% to ertapenem and 16.3% to both imipenem and meropenem among the carbapenems. Multidrug resistance was detected in 65.3% of isolates (32/49), and 18.4% were extensively drug-resistant. MLST testing of 13 MDR strains identified 13 different sequence types, the most dominant (15%) being ST147, followed by ST405 and ST268 (10% each). items.titel: Assessing the Influence of Tourism Development on Wildlife Conservation In GISHWATI-MUKURA National Park, Rwanda
items.samenvatting_bron: This study examined the influence of tourism development on wildlife conservation in Gishwati-Mukura National Park, Rwanda. It specifically assessed the influence of income creation, community-based tourism activities, and ecotourism activities on wildlife conservation. A descriptive research design was employed, targeting a population of 475 individuals, from whom a sample of 217 respondents was selected. Primary data were collected using structured questionnaires, while secondary data were obtained through documentary review. Data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, including Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis. The findings indicated that income creation, community-based tourism activities, and ecotourism activities were positively and significantly associated with wildlife conservation. The regression results showed positive effects of income creation (β = 0.428, p < 0.001), community-based tourism activities (β = 0.372, p < 0.001), and ecotourism activities (β = 0.451, p < 0.001) on wildlife conservation. The model explained 76.1% of the variance in wildlife conservation, indicating substantial explanatory power. The findings suggest that tourism development, particularly through income-generating opportunities, community participation, and ecotourism, can contribute significantly to wildlife conservation. Strengthening community involvement and promoting environmentally responsible tourism practices may therefore enhance the cons

items.titel: Building Predictive Identity Threat Models Using Behavioral Biometrics and Zero Trust Cybersecurity Principles
items.samenvatting_bron: This review explores the integration of behavioral biometrics and Zero Trust cybersecurity principles in building predictive identity threat models for advanced cyber defense. As traditional perimeter-based security becomes increasingly ineffective against sophisticated identity-based attacks, the fusion of behavioral biometrics—such as keystroke dynamics, mouse movement, touchscreen behavior, and gait recognition—with Zero Trust frameworks offers a more dynamic and continuous method of user authentication and threat prediction. By leveraging machine learning algorithms to analyze behavioral patterns in real time, organizations can identify anomalies indicative of account compromise, insider threats, or unauthorized access. Zero Trust, which operates on the principle of “never trust, always verify,” ensures that every user and device is continuously authenticated, authorized, and validated based on risk context and behavioral insights. This paper synthesizes the state-of-the-art technologies, architectures, and analytical techniques underpinning predictive identity threat modeling. It also examines use cases across sectors, implementation challenges, and future directions for securing digital identities in an era of pervasive cyber threats.

items.titel: Groundwater Contamination in India: Regional Variations, Hydrogeochemical Controls, Health Risks, and Integrated Management Strategies
items.samenvatting_bron: Groundwater plays a critical role in meeting drinking and agricultural water demands in India. This review focuses on regional variations in groundwater quality, contamination sources, and remediation strategies. The evaluation encompasses pH, electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids, hardness, major ions, and contaminants including fluoride, arsenic, nitrate, and heavy metals. Results reveal significant regional variations, with contamination driven by intensive agriculture, industrial activities, mining, urbanization, and geological factors. Water Quality Index assessments indicate that while many groundwater sources meet drinking standards, numerous sites exceed permissible limits, requiring treatment. Contamination stems from both natural processes (mineral dissolution and rock–water interactions) and anthropogenic activities (fertilizer application, industrial effluents, domestic sewage, and mining operations). Health risk assessments demonstrate elevated noncarcinogenic risks in fluoride- and nitrate-affected areas, causing fluorosis, arsenicosis, methemoglobinemia, and other waterborne diseases. Various remediation approaches suitable for Indian conditions have been investigated, including membrane-based systems, electrochemical methods, adsorption techniques, and nature-based solutions. items.titel: Challenges and prospects of dead Li 0 reactivation in lithium metal batteries
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract High-energy-density lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs) are promising next-generation energy storage technologies. However, the continuous and irreversible inactive metallic Li (dead Li0) generation severely limits battery lifespans. Notably, reactivating dead Li0 in addition to reducing its formation is also crucial for achieving long-life LMBs. Though prototype strategies (e.g., electrochemical protocols, redox chemistry) have achieved partial reactivation of dead Li0, their feasibility in practical cells remains limited by the large proportion of dead Li0 that persists. Directly reconnecting exposed dead Li0 with electrodes by introducing external electronically conductive materials is a promising solution, yet it fails to achieve the expected reactivation. To achieve efficient reactivation of dead Li0, key procedures including Li-stripping-related issues (e.g., mass transport, ion/electron transfer), solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) evolution, and effective dead Li0 exposure should be concurrently considered. The answer may be obtained through in-depth mechanistic studies using advanced characterization techniques. Additionally, insights into dead Li0 reactivation can be gained from existing methods (e.g., high cutoff voltage, lower current density) and from detecting environmental changes around the reactivated dead Li0 to identify favorable conditions. items.titel: Data Annotation as Measurement
items.samenvatting_bron: Modern AI systems depend on annotated data, but annotation is rarely treated as the act of measurement that it is. Instead, annotation quality is commonly reduced to agreement: if multiple annotators assign the same annotation to a data instance, the annotations are taken to be high-quality. Yet agreement does not establish whether annotations validly capture the underlying concept they are meant to represent. In this paper, we argue that data annotation should be understood as a measurement problem. Like other forms of measurement, annotation requires defining a concept, operationalizing it through an instrument, applying that instrument, and evaluating the reliability and validity of the resulting measurements. Drawing on a literature review of annotation quality research (N=132) and semi-structured interviews with annotation team members (N=10), we develop a framework for diagnosing and correcting annotation issues. First, we map key decision points across annotation processes - including task design, annotator management, quality assessment, quality improvement, and adjudication - that shape annotation outcomes. Second, we identify five distinct sources of annotation issues: error, ambiguity, impossibility, subjectivity, and annotator identity. Annotation problems that appear similar at the level of outcomes often require different process-level interventions based on their sources. items.titel: Shaping the Future of Generative AI for Black Communities: A Frame Analysis of Public Discourse and Empirical Scholarly Research
items.samenvatting_bron: As generative AI (genAI) systems become embedded in education, employment, healthcare, and creative industries, the impact and engagement among marginalized groups have become both a widespread discourse and a focus in scholarly research. As a starting point, we examine public discourse and empirical research to explore the impact of genAI systems on Black communities. We conducted a systematic literature review (SLR) of 91 empirical papers alongside a media discourse frame analysis of 28 public resources, applying Entman's framing theory to map how each corpus defines problems, attributes causes, and proposes treatments. Our SLR reveals that scholarly research concentrates heavily on technical bias detection, reducing Blackness to measurable variables rather than engaging with cultural practices, structural conditions, or Black knowledge systems. Our frame analysis reveals that public discourse attributes genAI-related harm to historical and systemic forces, while scholarly research stops its causal accounts at the dataset and its treatment recommendations at technical reform. We demonstrate that this misalignment is structurally produced: anti-Blackness operates simultaneously across both registers, generating a shared evacuation of Black epistemic agency. We argue for frame analysis as an AI ethics methodology capable of surfacing what technical evaluation forecloses.

items.titel: Watermelon vine as dual-functional additive in ecological porous concrete
items.samenvatting_bron: Ecological porous concrete (EPC) is constrained by a persistent trade-off: the dense cementitious matrix required for strength reduces porosity and generates a highly alkaline pore environment (pH > 11) inimical to plant growth. To address this, the present study investigates watermelon vine (WV), an abundant agricultural waste, as a dual-functional additive that simultaneously provides physical reinforcement and chemical alkalinity regulation. An integrated orthogonal array–response surface methodology–entropy-weighted TOPSIS framework was established for multi-objective mix optimisation. WV content was identified as the dominant factor governing pore pH, reducing it to 7.6 at an optimal dosage of 3 wt% within 14 days. The optimised mix—comprising 16–20 mm coarse aggregate, 20 wt% fly ash, a water-to-binder ratio of 0.26, and 3 wt% WV—achieved a compressive strength of 10.4 MPa and an effective porosity of 27.7%, with compressive strength remaining stable at 60 d. Scanning electron microscopy revealed a dense interfacial transition zone containing crystalline products morphologically consistent with calcium oxalate, and plant germination tests confirmed vegetation establishment exceeding 80% coverage within 60 days. These converging lines of evidence support an in-situ acid–base neutralisation mechanism, positioning WV as a viable, low-cost functional resource for sustainable construction.

items.titel: Quantifying the contribution of vegetation layer uncertainty to simulated forest fuels treatment placement
items.samenvatting_bron: Background Western US forests face rising high-severity fire risk motivating increased investment in forest management. The high cost of treatments and vast areas needing work require efficient resource allocation. Forest landscape models can help scale up analysis and support management, but underlying uncertainties can limit their utility. Aims We examined uncertainty in the initial forest input layer, quantifying the error and determining how much field data are needed to produce outputs suitable for informing management. Methods We created eight initial forest layers using various sample sizes and selection methods, ran 50-year simulations and compared outputs. We also resampled model outputs from 100 to 500 m resolution and evaluated the effects. Key results Stratified sampling stabilized errors and allowed using smaller sample sizes relative to random sampling, and coarser resolution resampling reduced errors while retaining key information. Combining these strategies produced similar outputs using all and only 25% of the data. Conclusions Combining stratified sampling with output coarsening reduces data demands while maintaining analytical rigor, enabling more actionable guidance for management planning. Implications This work advances the operational use of landscape models as a decision-support tool, allowing managers to scale up planning by integrating model outputs with expert knowledge and reducing reliance on labor-intensive field inventories.

items.titel: Emergency Response and Management of Pandemic Disasters and Their Environmental Dimensions: A Review of Lessons from COVID-19 in Bangladesh
items.samenvatting_bron: Pandemics are disasters whose causes and consequences are both rooted in the environment, yet emergency management and environmental management are usually reviewed apart. This narrative review synthesizes 74 documents published between 2008 and 2026, comprising peer-reviewed studies, reports of intergovernmental and national agencies, and selected news and NGO records, to examine the emergency response to COVID-19 in Bangladesh, with the European Union as a comparator, and to connect that response to its environmental dimensions. Bangladesh confirmed its first cases on 8 March 2020 and by mid-2025 had recorded more than 2.05 million cases and about 29,500 deaths. The early response was weakened by late and poorly coordinated decisions, limited testing, about 0.7 intensive-care beds per 100,000 people, shortages of protective equipment and weak risk communication, although two-dose vaccination coverage later reached about 70%. Environmentally, nitrogen dioxide over Dhaka fell by roughly two-thirds during the 2020 lockdown, but the gain was temporary, whereas at least 14,500 tonnes of health-care waste were generated nationally in April 2020 alone and only about 7% of COVID-19-related waste was properly managed. Cyclone Amphan and the 2020 monsoon floods struck during the lockdown and created compound emergencies, while disrupted food supply chains and tourism deepened livelihood losses. items.titel: Deep learning for large-scale mapping of coffee cultivation in Minas Gerais, Brazil
items.samenvatting_bron: Despite being the world's largest coffee producer, the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais still lacks up-to-date methodologies for the remote mapping of its coffee fields, largely due to strong regional heterogeneity in biophysical conditions. To help closing this gap, this study produces a state-level map of coffee plantations using deep learning applied to Sentinel-2 imagery. We evaluate three models for semantic segmentation: Single U-Net, Multi-Region U-Net, and GAN-based U-Net. A key innovation is a multitemporal inference strategy using Sentinel-2 images from 2020 to 2024, combined with a temporal filter incorporating agronomic knowledge of coffee cultivation cycles, to improve the identification of recently pruned or newly planted fields. We find that Multi-Region U-Net achieved the highest accuracy and was applied statewide, detecting 915 thousand ha of coffee in 2023. Our results demonstrate the potential of deep learning for scalable agricultural mapping and monitoring of large and diverse geographies.

items.titel: CropRotationViz: An open-source R framework for multi-scale crop rotation analysis and visualization
items.samenvatting_bron: Crop rotation analysis is fundamental to understanding agricultural landscape dynamics, yet the complexity of multi-annual, spatially explicit agricultural data presents significant analytical challenges. A key difficulty lies in tracking field parcels whose boundaries change over time through administrative splits, mergers, or reorganizations. This process requires robust spatial intersection approaches that can reconcile multi-temporal polygon geometries. Here, we present CropRotationViz, an open-source R package that provides a detailed framework for processing, analyzing, and visualizing crop rotation patterns across multiple spatial and temporal scales. The package implements a modular architecture consisting of (i) a spatial processing pipeline with automated data validation, crop nomenclature standardization through a customizable crop classification aggregation tool, and geometric handling of temporal field boundary changes through multi-year polygon intersection, (ii) interactive multi-annual flow and diversity visualizations, including Sankey diagram and structural diversity mapping, and environmental context integration, and (iii) three distinct visualization interfaces optimized for different analytical needs: a dynamic rendering mode for detailed exploration, a pre-rendered fast visualization mode for rapid regional comparisons, and a field-level interface for individual parcel inspection. items.titel: Possibilities for strengthening nature experiences and nature stewardship in the ‘not yet engaged’
items.samenvatting_bron: It is commonly argued that encouraging people to spend time in nature and appreciate nature is an important conduit for encouraging engagement in conservation stewardship actions. However, there is limited data available to help us understand how those ‘not yet engaged’ in conservation actually perceive nature-based settings and possibilities for nature stewardship. Here we address this gap by recruiting ‘not yet engaged’ individuals and providing guided nature experiences, followed by in-situ interviews to examine participant perceptions of these nature experiences and stewardship actions. Qualitative analysis integrated Kellert’s value typology and Value‑Beliefs‑Norm theory to assess how nature was valued, and ‘ingredients’ for stewardship action. We found that all participants described a positive appreciation of nature, reflected by naturalistic and aesthetic value orientations. However, participants were less likely to demonstrate other ingredients for stewardship, including awareness of actions that they could perform, and sense of responsibility or moral obligation to take specific actions. These findings suggest that programs aiming to promote conservation actions should not rely on encouraging nature appreciation in isolation, but also foster awareness of available actions and a sense of personal responsibility.

items.titel: Integrating free-living amoebae into climate-microbiome and One Health frameworks
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate change is altering microbial ecosystems at a global scale, yet the role of free-living amoebae within these shifting microbiomes remains incompletely understood. Free-living amoebae occupy soil, water, air, and built environments, where they contribute to microbial diversity, regulate nutrient cycling, and host diverse bacterial, fungal, and viral microorganisms. As temperature, moisture, and land-use patterns change, amoebal behaviour and their associated microbiomes may shift in ways that may affect soil fertility, water quality, microbial network stability, and the persistence of opportunistic pathogens. Through grazing, amoebae regulate bacterial turnover and mineral nutrient release from microbial biomass, providing a mechanistic link between nutrient cycling and plant accessible nutrient pools that underpin soil fertility. Understanding these dynamics is essential for planetary microbiome research and for strengthening One Health approaches that link environmental, animal, and human health. Herein, we discuss free-living amoebae in the context of climate change, the planetary microbiome, and One Health, and consider how their ecological roles may relate to broader shifts in microbial systems. We synthesise current evidence linking free-living amoebae to climate-responsive microbiome dynamics and propose their inclusion within planetary microbiome and One Health frameworks as responsive ecological indicators. items.titel: Load- versus concentration-based water quality metrics: Field assessment of permeable pavement and filter drain under Mediterranean rainfall in Valencia, Spain
items.samenvatting_bron: Study Region Valencia, Spain. Study Focus Two full-scale Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SUDS), a permeable pavement (PP) and a filter drain (FD), were monitored over one year at a residential street in Valencia under Mediterranean rainfall conditions. Hydraulic and water-quality performance were evaluated using concentration-based (Event Mean Concentration, EMC) and mass-based (Pollutant Mass Loading, PML) indicators. Rainfall, flow, and water quality were monitored at a conventional gully (CG) as a reference point and at both SUDS outlets across 14 rainfall events. Parameters included conventional pollutants (TSS, COD, BOD, TN, TP), 12 trace metals and metalloids, hydrocarbon fractions, and 16 PAHs. New Hydrological Insights for the Region Both systems attenuated runoff consistently, with volumetric efficiencies of 24–100% (mean: PP 57%, FD 65%) and no measured overflow for events below 10 mm, extending to 30 mm for FD. Concentration-based efficiencies were moderate and event-dependent, with occasional negative values for TSS, Cr and Ag at PP. Mass-based indicators revealed consistently higher reductions for most pollutants (SOL: 65–95%), even when outlet EMCs exceeded those at CG, indicating that volume reduction drives pollutant export reduction in highly retentive systems. A general first-flush tendency was observed across the 20 analysed pollutants. These findings indicate that, in highly retentive systems, EMC-based assessments alone can understate SUDS performance

items.titel: Knowledge uprooted: Transimperial forestry and the hiring of foreign experts in the Dutch East Indies, 1920s–1930s
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract This article examines the global networks underpinning colonial forestry in the Dutch East Indies in the interwar period. In the aftermath of the First World War, a renewed surge towards the internationalisation of the forest sciences served to open up imperial knowledge systems to a wider pool of outside expertise. This provided opportunities for smaller, thus far underresearched parties like the Nordic states, as explored here through a case study of a group of international foresters employed by the Dutch colonial administration in the 1930s. The article combines transimperial and global history approaches into a multisite analysis of both the scholarly exchanges that led to their initial hiring and their subsequent on-the-ground work in the colony. It is argued that an actor-oriented interrogation of the practical networks and internal frictions of colonial knowledge work reveals the hesitant emergence of a multilateral system that anticipated the post-1945 regime of international development.

items.titel: Biochemical Markers, Physiological Resilience, and Smart Health Monitoring: A Multidisciplinary Review of Human Physical Performance and Health Maintenance

This review article synthesizes recent multidisciplinary empirical scholarship to establish an integrated framework for athletic performance, occupational wellness, and digital biometric health tracking. Third, we review technological advancements in smart healthcare management systems (Livingword et al., 2026) and introduce advanced quantitative variance modeling—specifically Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (ARCH) and Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (EGARCH) architectures—to model time-series volatility in physiological exertion and hea

items.titel: Correlação entre as Práticas Ambientais, Sociais e de Governança (ESG) e o Ecoturismo na Gestão de Parques Nacionais Brasileiros
items.samenvatting_bron: Objetivo – Analisar as práticas ambientais, sociais e de governança (ESG) correlacionadas ao ecoturismo na gestão dos Parques Nacionais (PARNA) brasileiros, sob a perspectiva de seus gestores. Desenho/metodologia/abordagem – A pesquisa adotou abordagem quantitativa, de caráter exploratório e descritivo, utilizando um questionário estruturado (survey) com questões em escala tipo Likert de cinco pontos. O instrumento foi enviado aos 75 gestores dos PARNA brasileiros, obtendo-se 23 respostas válidas. Os dados foram analisados no software MAXQDA por meio da correlação de Spearman entre os critérios de ecoturismo e os eixos ambiental, social e de governança do ESG. Resultados – Os resultados evidenciaram associações positivas entre as práticas de ecoturismo e os três eixos do ESG, com destaque para correlações muito significativas e altamente significativas relacionadas ao eixo ambiental. As análises indicam que práticas de conservação, educação ambiental, governança e participação social podem atuar de forma integrada no fortalecimento do uso público e da gestão dos Parques Nacionais. Implicações práticas – O instrumento desenvolvido apresenta potencial para apoiar o ICMBio na estruturação de uma ferramenta de diagnóstico das práticas ESG nos Parques Nacionais, subsidiando o planejamento, o monitoramento da gestão e a definição de prioridades para o aperfeiçoamento do uso público. Originalidade/valor – O estudo amplia a discussão sobre a aplicação da abordagem ESG em áreas natura

items.titel: Mitogenomic characterisation of non-native freshwater snails in Australia: Implications for biosecurity and trematode vector surveillance.

items.titel: Episodic High‐Latitude Occurrence of Walleye Pollock ( Gadus chalcogrammus ) in the Central Arctic Ocean Associated With Warm Subsurface Conditions: Multi‐Year Environmental DNA and Larval Evidence
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Episodic high‐latitude occurrences of subarctic fish due to Arctic warming present significant challenges for managing high‐latitude ecosystems. In this study, we present four consecutive years (2021–2024) of integrated environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring and larval surveys for walleye pollock ( Gadus chalcogrammus ) conducted aboard the Korean icebreaker IBR/V Araon in the Chukchi Sea (CS) and Central Arctic Ocean (CAO). Of the 342 eDNA samples from 180 stations (55°N–76°N, spanning the Bering Sea, CS, and CAO, including underway surface‐pump stations), walleye pollock eDNA was detected in 25 samples (7.3%), with annual detection rates ranging from 2.8% to 13.2%. In 2024, eDNA was detected at 75°58′N, representing the northernmost molecular record for this species and extending beyond the previous northernmost trawl record (75.44°N). Larvae were collected in 2021 ( n = 5; standard length [SL]: 3.4–5.1 mm) and 2022 ( n = 3; SL: 9.7–14.6 mm) but were absent in 2023 and 2024 despite peak eDNA detection, indicating that northward pollock occurrence has not yet resulted in successful local reproduction. eDNA‐positive stations exhibited significantly warmer bottom temperatures than negative stations ( U = 2845, p = 0.0012; odds ratio [OR] = 1.74/°C [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.25–2.44]). items.titel: Hidden Microbiome of Mining Environments: Implications for Occupational Health, Bioaerosol Exposure, and Antimicrobial Resistance
items.samenvatting_bron: Mining environments are extreme subsurface ecosystems characterized by elevated concentrations of metals and minerals, limited light, and high particulate loads. Occupational health research in mining has traditionally emphasized physical and chemical hazards, whereas biological exposures remain less well-characterized. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on mining-associated microbial communities, bioaerosols, occupational exposure, respiratory health, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The literature search covered PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from database inception through August 2026. Evidence from coal, uranium, metal mining, acid mine drainage, and mine dust environments indicates that geochemical conditions and mining activities shape microbial communities. Drilling, blasting, excavation, and ore transport can aerosolize microbial cells, spores, and dust-associated microbial components, creating plausible inhalation pathways. Metal-rich environments may also favor persistence and co-selection of metal- and antibiotic-resistance determinants within environmental microbial communities. Metagenomic sequencing and environmental DNA approaches have expanded detection of microbial diversity, functional genes, and environmental resistomes. However, environmental detection does not establish microbial viability, effective worker exposure, transmission, or disease causation. items.titel: Habitat-use flexibility may promote the spread of Asian weatherloaches in Europe
items.samenvatting_bron: Asian weatherloaches have expanded their range across Europe, potentially increasing competitive pressure on the conservation-dependent native European weatherfish Misgurnus fossilis . Because interspecific interactions are potentially mediated by benthic habitat use, we quantified substrate choice of native European and invasive Asian weatherloaches in a replicated laboratory two-way choice experiment. Individual fish were tested in three sediment combinations (gravel/sand, gravel/mud, sand/mud) with four 60-min replicates per treatment and individual fish. Habitat use was quantified as the proportional time spent on each substrate and analysed using a linear mixed-effects model. Habitat use differed significantly between invasive and native loach species. Post-hoc comparisons and effect sizes (Hedges’ g) indicated a pronounced divergence for muddy substrate, with native Misgurnus fossilis showing substantially higher mud use than Asian weatherloaches, while differences in selection for gravel and sand were small. These findings support the adaptive flexibility hypothesis by indicating a more generalist substrate-use pattern in invasive Asian weatherloaches relative to the mud-specialised European weatherfish. From a management perspective, conserving and restoring structurally complex muddy floodplain habitats may provide a competitive refuge for European weatherfish and should be prioritised alongside targeted monitoring of Asian weatherloach spread and habitat overlap.

items.titel: Biology and conservation of the European mudminnow (Umbra krameri Walbaum, 1792): an update of the monograph 30 years after the first international workshop
items.samenvatting_bron: During the three decades following the publication of the first comprehensive monograph on the European mudminnow ( Umbra krameri Walbaum, 1792), knowledge of the species’ biology, distribution, genetics, ecology, and conservation has expanded substantially. In several countries, a dynamic distribution pattern has become apparent, with many local populations seemingly disappearing while new populations continue to be documented. However, many of these newly recorded occurrences likely represent previously overlooked remnant populations rather than genuine range expansions. Despite the uncertainty associated with detectability, the overall distribution pattern of U. krameri clearly reflects a large-scale process of range contraction and habitat fragmentation across most of its native range. Recent phylogeographic and population genetic studies have fundamentally improved understanding of the species by revealing pronounced drainage-based structuring, limited contemporary gene flow, and the existence of distinct evolutionarily significant units (ESUs). At the same time, the development of genomic resources, complete mitogenome assemblies, and environmental DNA (eDNA) approaches has created entirely new opportunities for monitoring and conservation. items.titel: Small, isolated, and critically endangered: conservation genetics of the European mudminnow (Umbra krameri) in Austria
items.samenvatting_bron: Floodplain specialist fishes have undergone disproportionate declines across Europe due to river regulation and groundwater alteration. The European mudminnow ( Umbra krameri ), now Critically Endangered in Austria, persists naturally in only two isolated populations (Fadenbach, Jesuitenbach). Field surveys were combined with microsatellite analyses to assess population structure and genetic diversity in both wild populations and in four ex situ stocks established from Fadenbach. Wild populations were strongly differentiated, indicating prolonged isolation without contemporary gene flow. Despite marked demographic fluctuations and recent habitat desiccation, both populations retained moderate levels of heterozygosity and showed no significant signal of a recent bottleneck. Whereas the estimated contemporary effective population size was critically low for the Fadenbach population, no robust estimate could be obtained for the Jesuitenbach population. All ex situ populations derived exclusively from Fadenbach and collectively retained their allelic diversity, yet showed significant divergence from one another due to founder effects and drift. These results thus identify two genetically distinct conservation units and reveal acute vulnerability masked by currently stable diversity metrics. items.titel: Integrating land-use dynamics, water quality, and multi-criteria ecological suitability for fish sanctuary prioritization in three major river basins of Bangladesh
items.samenvatting_bron: Riverine ecosystems in monsoon-dominated regions are increasingly constrained by interacting pressures from land-use change, hydrological alteration, and water-quality degradation, yet these drivers are rarely assessed within a unified framework. This study presents a reproducible, basin-scale framework integrating multi-season (monsoon–dry) land-use dynamics (2000–2020), hydrochemical assessment (including nutrients and trace metals), and GIS-based Multi-Criteria ecological modeling to delineate fish sanctuary suitability across the Ganges–Padma, Brahmaputra–Jamuna, and Barak–Meghna basins of Bangladesh. Results showed a 1.5% decline in monsoon water extent, 12.7% decline in the mapped monsoon vegetation class, and a 25% increase in dry-season vegetation, indicating reduced floodplain connectivity and progressive habitat simplification. Water quality further constrained habitat suitability, with 37.5% of site–season observations classified as poor, very poor, or unsuitable, frequent dissolved oxygen concentrations below 5 mg L − 1 , and localized heavy metal concentrations exceeding guideline thresholds. The integrated Suitability Index identified only 4.9% of the landscape as highly suitable, characterized by perennial water depth, strong connectivity, and low pollution levels. Overall, the findings demonstrate that habitat degradation in large river basins is driven by the combined effects of landscape and hydrological change and hydrochemical stress. items.titel: Assessing fish biodiversity and community structure in the Ganjiang River using eDNA metabarcoding
items.samenvatting_bron: Hydropower development has emerged as a major driver of global environmental change, causing significant ecological damage to freshwater ecosystems and threatening aquatic biodiversity. However, the impact of cascade dams on fish communities in large river systems remains poorly understood, particularly in biodiversity hotspots such as China. Here, we used environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding to assess the spatiotemporal patterns of fish diversity and community structure in the Ganjiang River, the largest tributary of the Yangtze River, in relation to cascade hydropower development. We collected water samples from 19 sites along the main stem and major tributaries in both wet and dry seasons, and analyzed the eDNA data using high-throughput sequencing and advanced bioinformatics pipelines. Our results revealed significant seasonal and spatial variations in fish diversity and community composition, with lower species richness and distinct assemblages in the impounded sections upstream of the dams compared to the downstream reaches. The fish communities were strongly influenced by environmental factors such as water temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, and nutrients, which exhibited complex interactions with dam operation and land use practices. Spatial scale analyses further indicated that the impact of dams on fish diversity was most pronounced at the local scale, but also detectable at the regional scale. items.titel: Changes in the distribution of the European mudminnow (Umbra krameri Walbaum, 1792) in Hungary over the last 50 years
items.samenvatting_bron: The European mudminnow ( Umbra krameri Walbaum, 1792) is a relict wetland fish endemic to the Danube Basin, with Hungary representing the core of its historical distribution. We compiled published faunistic records, grey literature and standardised field-survey data from 1975–2025 to quantify long-term distribution changes across 12 Hungarian geographic regions and 200 documented localities. Confirmed persistent populations occur at 45.5% of historical localities (91 sites), including 17 “large” and 74 “small” populations. An additional 15 sites (7.5%) show only occasional recent records, whereas the European mudminnow has disappeared from 44% of its historically known localities. Most extant populations remain small and spatially fragmented. The Danube–Tisza Interfluve historically contained the highest number of localities (n = 57) and exhibited the greatest absolute loss (33 disappeared sites), primarily associated with hydrological degradation. In contrast, the Fertő–Hanság–Szigetköz Region currently represents the most important north-western refuge (21 persistent populations, including three large populations), whereas the Zámoly Basin is regionally extinct. Across all localities, invasion by the Amur sleeper ( Perccottus glenii Dybowski, 1877) (35% of sites) and documented desiccation (30.5%) were the two most frequently recorded threat categories. items.titel: A sample-to-identification workflow to monitor animal and plant biodiversity using metabarcoding and real time analysis
items.samenvatting_bron: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a transformative tool for biodiversity monitoring, offering a non-invasive means to detect and identify species across various ecosystems. However, despite its potential, current eDNA methodologies have significant limitations, including limited sensitivity, restriction to a specific taxonomic group, lengthy processing times, the need for specialized laboratory conditions and equipment, as well as computational bottlenecks in equipment, connectivity, and algorithms. Overcoming these limitations is crucial for the real-time monitoring of a high number of taxa in field-based scenarios. Here we present an integrated eDNA workflow from extraction to data analysis that mitigates several of these challenges through several technical innovations. Our approach adapts the Tagsteady protocol to Nanopore sequencing, integrates multiplex PCR for simultaneous plant and animal detection, and introduces RTBioScan, a real-time analysis pipeline employing hierarchical basecalling and OTU-level consensus generation to achieve high-accuracy taxonomic assignments during sequencing. Using a single set of universal primers, we integrate metabarcoding and barcoding into a cohesive protocol, utilizing universal markers for both animals and plants (cytochrome oxidase 1 region, COI, and Internal Transcribed Spacer 2, ITS2). items.titel: Distribution, habitat, and population dynamics of the European weatherfish (Misgurnus fossilis L., 1758) in the north-easternmost part of Germany
items.samenvatting_bron: This study analyses a distribution database of fishes and cyclostomes from the German federal state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and evaluates a monitoring programme initiated in 2008, with a focus on the ecology of the European weatherfish. Over 35 years, the species was recorded across nearly the entire state, but it was rarely found in high abundances. While the species’ natural habitats have largely disappeared as a result of land cultivation, the weatherfish is now predominantly found in extensive, human-made drainage systems, where it co-exists with other fish species adapted to warm, oxygen-poor conditions. Since 1990, the frequency of detections indicates a stable population status. To date, ten monitored populations normally exhibited low population densities, often below one individual per 100 m 2 . However, several populations occasionally exhibited densities far exceeding the average. These temporary increases were primarily driven by a single age class, indicating irregular reproduction or recruitment dynamics. This pattern should be considered when assessing the species’ conservation status according to the EU Habitats Directive. Furthermore, populations exhibiting such dynamics are more susceptible to local extinction than those with continuous reproduction. Therefore, maintaining metapopulation connectivity is critical for effective conservation. items.titel: The Development and Application of Environmental DNA (eDNA) Methods for Hornbill Monitoring
items.samenvatting_bron: This research demonstrated the applicability of eDNA for detecting elusive hornbills, addressing the limitations of traditional field surveys. Focused on Anthracoceros albirostris, the research performed key investigations into qPCR assay development, sampling protocols, and remote storage method that align with hornbill ecology and nesting behavior in tropical forests. These findings were synthesized into a preliminary protocol guide, providing a practical framework for practitioners to implement the eDNA approach for monitoring hornbills in regions where molecular monitoring remains underutilized.

items.titel: Assessing the use of inland wetlands by fishes in the Lower Tagus Basin, Portugal
items.samenvatting_bron: Although inland wetlands are among the most important and impacted biodiversity hotspots worldwide, they remain poorly assessed. This is particularly concerning in regions harboring endangered endemic species and facing strong anthropogenic pressures, such as the Lower Tagus Basin in Portugal. Here we aimed to assess the use of inland wetlands in the Lower Tagus basin by native and non-native fishes and examine the environmental factors influencing community structure. Using Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery and the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), we identified 409 water surfaces, 30 of which with potential to sustain fishes over time. We surveyed 11 wetlands for fishes using a standardized, multi-gear sampling approach. We found that local fish communities were dominated by non-native species, with deep, paleopotamic wetlands (e.g., Golegã and Gouxa) tending to function as reservoirs for Largemouth Bass ( Micropterus nigricans ) and Pumpkinseed Sunfish ( Lepomis gibbosus ). Conversely, parapotamic wetlands directly connected to the Tagus River (e.g., Setil and Sto. Estevão) appeared to provide migration corridors for Thin Lip Grey Mullet ( Chelon ramada ) and shallow wetlands (e.g., Caniceiras and Granho) serve as refuges for native and threatened Lisbon Arched-mouth Nase ( Iberochondrostoma olisiponense ), European Eel ( Anguilla anguilla ), and Southern Iberian Spined Loach ( Cobitis paludica ). items.titel: Stemflow as a Storm-Driven Pathway for Fungal eDNA Transport
items.samenvatting_bron: Stemflow transports water and biological material from forest canopies to the stem base, yet fungal studies of this flux have largely relied on microscopy of conidia. We used ITS2 metabarcoding to characterize fungal environmental DNA (eDNA) in stemflow from 15 trees – five each of American beech (Fagus grandifolia), sugar maple (Acer saccharum), and tulip poplar (Liriodendron tulipifera) in a closed-canopy forest in northeastern Ohio, USA. Stemflow was sampled during eight rain events in the leafless season (November 2024–May 2025), along with simulated bark and gutter washes to assess near-collar and collector signals. Natural stemflow communities were compositionally distinct from both controls and occupied greater ordination space. Ascomycota dominated across all samples, with Parafenestella, Cytospora, Microcera, Nectria, and Aureobasidium among the most abundant resolved genera and 13 of the 25 most abundant taxa differed significantly among host species. Woody-plant-associated endophytes, canker fungi, and saprobes dominated ecological guild composition. Storm event explained 28.6% of taxonomic variation, host tree species 24.1%, and their interaction 10.0%. Guild composition was more strongly structured by host species (35.4%) than storm event (20.4%). Lichenized fungi and lichen-associated fungi were detected. items.titel: Marine ecosystem ecology at a crossroads
items.samenvatting_bron: Research in marine ecosystem ecology increasingly integrates biodiversity status and trends, ecosystem functioning, and human pressures. Understanding how marine biodiversity supports ecosystem functioning remains central to the field, while growing concern over ecosystem condition has shifted attention towards relationships between human pressures and ecological responses. These established questions are increasingly complemented by the need to anticipate climate-driven ecosystem transformations and translate ecological knowledge into effective conservation and management. Resilience – the capacity of ecosystems to persist and maintain their state and functions through resistance to and recovery from disturbance – has therefore become a central scientific priority under intensifying cumulative pressures. Major challenges for the coming decade include ecological non-stationarity, rapidly expanding data volumes, erosion of traditional expertise, uneven uptake of technological advances, and restoration under changing environmental conditions. Meeting these challenges requires marine ecosystem ecology to keep pace with global change while improving the transfer of knowledge into policy and management. Here, we identify these priorities and outline pathways towards more predictive, integrated, and decision-relevant marine ecosystem science.

items.titel: The utility of eDNA monitoring eukaryote communities for catchment assessments
items.samenvatting_bron: This study tested the efficacy of using environmental DNA biodiversity data as biological indicators of water quality using the Great Barrier Reef catchment as a case study. We passively sampled two catchment areas for ecosystem assessment with citizen scientists. Environmental DNA samples were collected in parallel with water quality sampling (nutrients, pesticides, sediments) to investigate trends between environmental parameters and eDNA eukaryote community composition. Sampling took place on three occasions.

items.titel: Recent advances in understanding the impact of microplastics on bacterial antibiotic resistance: mechanisms, evidence gaps, and One Health implications
items.samenvatting_bron: Microplastic (MP) pollution and bacterial antimicrobial resistance are converging public health concerns. MPs provide persistent, mobile surfaces that can transport antibiotic-resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). After aging and conditioning, MPs can develop biofilms in which resistance determinants accumulate, persist, and undergo horizontal transfer. This review conceptualizes MPs as mobile evolutionary interfaces and examines how particle properties and environmental conditions shape these processes. MP-associated biofilms increase cell density, retain extracellular DNA, and promote intercellular contact, facilitating plasmid conjugation and, in some experimental systems, transformation. Adsorbed antibiotics, metals, biocides, and plastic additives may exert selective or co-selective pressures, while oxidative stress, membrane perturbation, and SOS responses may alter gene-transfer potential. Studies of conventional and biodegradable MPs report enrichment of ARGs, MGEs, virulence-associated genes, and potential pathogens, however, neither enrichment nor biodegradability alone establishes health risk. Reports effects vary with polymer chemistry, particle size, concentration, aging, and microbial community composition. items.titel: Distributed Leadership for Mission Integration
items.samenvatting_bron: As Catholic and Vincentian institutions navigate increasing religious pluralism, declining numbers of vowed religious, and changing expectations about leadership, new models of mission leadership are needed. This article proposes distributed leadership for mission as a framework for sustaining Catholic and Vincentian identity in higher education. Drawing from the history of Vincent de Paul, Louise de Marillac, and the Vincentian Family, as well as contemporary scholarship on leadership and organizational effectiveness, it argues that mission is best carried forward through intentional networks of leaders who share responsibility for cultivating institutional culture and advancing a common purpose. The article explores the theoretical foundations of distributed leadership, highlights the importance of relationships, community, compassion, and ongoing formation, and identifies practices that foster mission integration across an institution of Catholic higher education. It concludes that distributed leadership reflects contemporary organizational realities, the emerging character and needs of the Catholic Church, and the deepest traditions of the Vincentian charism, offering a sustainable path for mission effectiveness in the twenty-first century.

items.titel: Land carbon sinks in the European Union are not keeping pace with carbon neutrality expectations
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract The European Union has substantially reduced greenhouse-gas emissions since 1990, yet the land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF) sink has not strengthened in parallel. The EU-27 LULUCF balance was approximately −231 MtCO₂e in 2024, while the latest Member State projections indicate a remaining gap of 40–55 MtCO₂e to the binding −310 MtCO₂e target for 2030. Here, we synthesise recent assessments to examine the drivers of this weakening in the land carbon sink and their implications for the effectiveness of climate mitigation policy. Declining forest growth, increased harvesting, climate-driven disturbances, and rising biomass demand reduce net carbon uptake, with one 2040 GLOBIOM sensitivity analysis indicating an approximately 100 MtCO₂e reduction in the LULUCF sink under an additional 20 Mtoe of woody-biomass demand. Concurrently, the EU inventory reported 52.7% uncertainty in the 2022 LULUCF level and 29.4% uncertainty in its trend, while important soil-carbon dynamics remain incompletely represented. These findings indicate that current climate policy frameworks implicitly assume stable, scalable, and rapidly deliverable land-based removals, whereas land carbon sinks are dynamic, disturbance-sensitive, and constrained by biophysical limits. items.titel: Effects of natural environmental drivers and different mobile bottom-contact fishing intensity on infauna communities in NATURA 2000 sites in the German Exclusive Economic Zone of the North Sea
items.samenvatting_bron: Three marine protected areas, i.e., Borkum Reef Ground, Sylt Outer Reef, and Dogger Bank, have been established within the European NATURA 2000 program in the German Exclusive Economic Zone of the North Sea. Within them, we analysed the effect of the varying impact of mobile bottom-contact fishing on infauna communities in selected focus areas as a baseline study prior to the exclusion of mobile bottom-contact fishing since 2023. The three focus areas varied significantly in sediment composition and depth. The mobile bottom-contact fishing intensity was lowest at Borkum Reef Ground, but revealed decreasing gradients at Sylt Outer Reef and Dogger Bank. The infauna communities in the three focus areas were significantly different. Gradients in sediment composition, e.g. sand, mud, gravel and shell contents, revealed significant relationships with the infauna communities in the three areas. But on a small spatial scale also the gradients of mobile bottom-contact fishing intensity correlated significantly with the variations of the infauna communities at Sylt Outer Reef and Dogger Bank. The common agreement of the European Commission for the exclusion of mobile bottom-contact fishing in parts of Borkum Reef Ground and Sylt Outer Reef since 2023 and of Dogger Bank since 2025 will provide the opportunity to study the recovery of the infauna communities in these areas from mobile bottom-contact fishing in future.

items.titel: Assessment of 226Ra and 228Ra activity concentrations in drinking water sources along Ghana’s coastal communities
items.samenvatting_bron: This study reports a screening-level radiological assessment of drinking water sources – sachet water, tap water, borehole water and river water – across the Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions of Ghana. Activity concentrations of 226 Ra and 228 Ra were measured by high-purity germanium (HPGe) gamma spectrometry in 244 samples collected over one dry and one wet season, and screening-level committed effective doses were estimated for adult consumers. All sachet and tap water samples returned activity concentrations below the minimum detectable activity (MDA) of the method (0.12 Bq L − 1 for 226 Ra and 0.14 Bq L − 1 for 228 Ra) and are reported as < MDA. Because the 228 Ra MDA (0.14 Bq L − 1 ) is above the WHO guidance level for 228 Ra (0.1 Bq L − 1 ), compliance of these samples with the 228 Ra guidance level could not be demonstrated by the method used; a non-detect establishes only that the activity was below 0.14 Bq L − 1 . Treating both MDAs as upper bounds gives an upper-bound screening dose of 0.095 mSv y − 1 , which is just below – not well below – the WHO individual dose criterion of 0.1 mSv y − 1 . items.titel: Guardians of the Green: The Judiciary's Role in Environmental Protection and the Evolution of Environmental Jurisprudence in India
items.samenvatting_bron: This paper critically examines the part played by the Indian judiciary in the protection and preservation of the environment and in the development of environmental case law. It traces the history of environmental protection in India, with special reference to the constitutional provisions, judicial activism and the expansion of Public Interest Litigation (PIL). It studies how the courts have tried to balance the conflicting interests of industrial development and environmental sustainability, while recognising the right to a clean and healthy environment as an essential part of the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution. Focusing on the judicial development of environmental principles, the study examines how the Public Trust Doctrine, Sustainable Development, the Polluter Pays Principle and the Precautionary Principle have been applied in important judicial decisions. It also considers the importance of PIL in combating environmental degradation and examines key cases relating to mining, industrial pollution, hazardous activities and water contamination. items.titel: Circular Transformation in the Silk Sector: A Fuzzy Delphi–DEMATEL Analysis of Critical Factors
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT The circular transformation in the silk industry is crucial for enhancing resource efficiency and minimizing waste. Despite growing interest in circularity within the textile sector, the silk industry remains underexplored. This study addresses this gap by systematically assessing the barriers and enablers influencing circular economy adoption in silk. A two‐stage methodology was applied. First, a comprehensive literature review combined with expert input identified key factors, which were then validated using the fuzzy Delphi method (FDM) with 16 experts from industry and academia, resulting in nine barriers and 12 enablers. Next, the Decision‐Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) technique examined the prominence and causal relationships among these factors. Results indicate that lack of policy support from fashion brands, ineffective planning, and inadequate communication are the most significant barriers, while limited consumer awareness and high technology costs strongly influence other barriers. Key enablers include upcycling business models, rediscovery of silk knowledge, and waste material recovery. Resource efficiency culture, design for longevity, and traditional expertise act as causal drivers. The study provides actionable guidance for managers, policymakers, and researchers, offering practical and theoretical insights to advance circularity in silk.

items.titel: A source-to-sea decision-support framework for wet-weather wastewater load management: evidence from Jiaozhou Bay
items.samenvatting_bron: Coastal concentration compliance can overlook increased wastewater throughput during wet weather. items.titel: The Silent Spaces of Cultural Heritage: The Transformation of Archaeological Excavation Houses
items.samenvatting_bron: With the development of the discipline of archaeology, excavation houses emerged initially as temporary shelter solutions; over time, however, the extension of excavation periods, the diversification of working conditions, and the increase in interdisciplinary studies led them to evolve into more permanent and functional spaces. It is observed that excavation houses do not possess a fixed typology; rather, various spatial forms—from tents and school buildings to prefabricated structures, as well as historical and modern buildings—have been utilized for this purpose. Today, excavation houses have become multifunctional environments that not only serve as places of accommodation and work, but also enhance the quality of archaeological practice, support public awareness, and contribute to the transmission of cultural heritage. Excavation houses are addressed under two main categories—temporary and permanent accommodation—and, based on research and observations, these categories are further divided into subcategories and analyzed through examples. Results The estimates made suggests that about 75% of the world's value creation has its origin in natural resources, and about 2 / 3 of the value creation has its origin in finite, fossil natural resources, fossil energy, fossil metals, and fossil materials. Our results suggests that a system reconfiguration, including thorium-based technologies, would be required for making society last more than 1,000 generations. The most valuable resources in analysis are the energy resources, but these are partly dependent on the availability of technology metals and materials. Thorium appears to be the single most valuable energy resource on the list, provided thorium-based power plants are adopted, and based on the energy price.
