items.titel: Prioritizing climate-resilient housing recovery in conflict-affected Yemen: a district-level MCDA and uncertainty framework
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Yemen’s housing recovery requires choices among districts where flood exposure, conflict, displacement and humanitarian need overlap. This study develops a district-level multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework to identify districts that remain high priorities for early climate-resilient housing recovery under alternative assumptions. The model combines seven dimensions: flood hazard, human exposure, built exposure, climate stress, conflict fragility, displacement pressure and humanitarian severity. Four weighting scenarios are tested, and Monte Carlo perturbation examines rank stability when normalized inputs and scenario weights vary. The model does not estimate direct housing damage; it screens districts under combined physical and social pressures and compares the national ranking with heterogeneous city-level evidence. The highest-ranked districts are Ma’rib, Ma’rib City, Sirwah, Al Marawi’ah, Khur Maksar, Ad Durayhimi, Tuban and Bani Sa’d. Flood-gate, missing-data, internal-weight and sparse-RDT ablation tests preserve the leading pattern, although uncertainty increases near selection thresholds. The framework provides a transparent national screening tool for recovery sequencing, subject to local engineering assessment and stakeholder validation before implementation.

items.titel: FRAMEWORK DEVELOPMENT OF BIOPHILIC MODEL FOR CORPORATE BUILDINGS
items.samenvatting_bron: Environmental degradation and unorganized cities are rising issues because of a growing population in an era of fast globalization. People confronted a dilemma with denser and congested urban development, which highlighted the fragility of towns and their residents. There are no such rules that govern the general equilibrium of the ecosystem due to rising urbanization and unplanned cities. As a result, global temperatures will rise by 1.5 degrees Celsius by 2050. Rapid building has made a substantial impact on the natural world to meet the requirements of a rising population. It contributes to global warming by generating more than 30% of the world's emissions of greenhouse gases. Buildings are the largest energy consumers and equivalent to approximately 40% of all substantial energy sources for example nuclear energy, hydropower, and fossil fuels. Sustainable construction and development methods are being used to reduce negative consequences and create an environment that is more environmentally friendly. Applying biophilic design concepts in building construction to generate connections between individuals and the environment is one method of achieving sustainability. items.titel: When heat hits: Short-run saving and withdrawal behavior among microfinance clients in Benin
items.samenvatting_bron: Increased access to finance is widely viewed as a key driver to increase adaptive capacity in response to climate change. However, apart from limited studies on borrowing behavior, little is known about how exposure to extreme heat is associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. This study addresses this gap by investigating the short-run associations of unusual heat with microfinance clients’ saving and withdrawal behavior. In a case study, it combines geo-located temperature data with a unique dataset of around 50,000 clients of a leading Microfinance Institution (MFI) in Benin. Applying two-way fixed effects, seemingly unrelated regression, and ordinary least squares models, the study finds that exposure to extreme heat is heterogeneously associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. Specifically, non-agricultural clients show suggestive evidence of the accumulation of precautionary savings after extreme heat days in the preceding quarter, while extreme heat days are negatively associated with agricultural clients’ savings. Microfinance clients increase their withdrawals when exposed to extreme heat within the preceding quarter, but the association is not robust for agricultural clients’ withdrawals in response to an increase in annual extreme heat days. items.titel: Agronomic and Nutritional Perspectives on Vegetable Crops in Africa
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Vegetable production plays a crucial role in food security, nutrition, and livelihoods across Africa. Yet, it faces persistent challenges related to climate variability, water scarcity, soil degradation, and limited access to agricultural inputs. This review synthesizes current agronomic, nutritional, and socio‐economic perspectives on vegetable production systems in Africa, with a particular emphasis on sustainability and resilience. Key agronomic strategies, including improved irrigation practices, integrated nutrient management, and the use of biostimulants, are discussed as pathways to enhance productivity under resource‐constrained conditions. Agronomic practices are discussed in terms of their influence not only on crop productivity but also on nutritional composition, phytochemical accumulation, postharvest quality, and food safety, whereas the role of indigenous knowledge systems in supporting climate adaptation, soil health, biodiversity conservation, and low‐input farming practices is also considered. From a phytochemical and nutritional standpoint, African indigenous vegetables emerge as underutilized yet highly valuable crops, rich in vitamins, essential elements, and bioactive compounds with antioxidant and anti‐inflammatory properties. These attributes position vegetables not only as sources of nourishment but also as functional foods with the potential to address micronutrient deficiencies and reduce the burden of non‐communicable diseases. items.titel: EXPLORING VERTICAL GREENING SYSTEM FOR ENHANCING THERMAL COMFORT IN THE DESIGN OF POSTGRADUATE HOSTEL FOR GOMBE STATE UNIVERSITY, GOMBE, NIGERIA
items.samenvatting_bron: The concept of vertical greening systems has gained considerable attention in recent years as an innovative approach to enhancing thermal comfort within various built environments. This growing interest is rooted in the recognition of the substantial influence that greenery can exert on the microclimate of structures. The design of student hostels in general faces a significant challenge on thermal discomfort, intensified by high solar gain in the tropical savannah climate. Traditional building materials offer minimal insulation, leading to increased reliance on energy intensive cooling systems. In this regard, the integration of vertical greening systems presents an intriguing opportunity to not only improves the aesthetic appeal of the building but also to create a more comfortable and sustainable living environment for its occupants. By exploring the potential benefits and challenges associated with these systems, this research focuses on investigating the effectiveness of vertical greening systems in improving thermal comfort within the design of a postgraduate student hostel at Gombe State University. The study aims to evaluate the influence of these systems on creating a more comfortable living environment. The study employs a case study approach to analyze selected buildings. items.titel: THE NETWORKING OF AI-DRIVEN IMPROVED SANITATION ARCHITECTURE INNOVATIONS, STRATEGIES AND SOLUTIONS TOWARDS ODF IN BAUCHI BUILT ENVIRONMENT
items.samenvatting_bron: The quest for the pursuit of Open Defecation Free (ODF) status in Nigeria, particularly in states like Bauchi, has historically relied on conventional Community-Led Total Sanitation (CLTS) approaches. However, the sustainability of these interventions is often compromised by inadequate facility maintenance, poor design aesthetics, and lack of economic incentives. This paper explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and improved toilet architecture innovations as a transformative strategy for achieving and sustaining ODF in the Bauchi built environment. By leveraging AI-driven generative design, parametric modeling, and Internet of Things (IoT) predictive maintenance, architects and urban planners can develop culturally resonant, climate-resilient, and economically viable sanitation facilities. This research proposes a framework where AI algorithms analyze local topographical, climatic, and socio-cultural data to generate optimized architectural designs for public and communal toilets. Furthermore, the integration of AI-powered digital twins and smart sensors facilitates real-time monitoring of facility usage, structural integrity, and environmental impact. The findings suggest that AI-driven architectural innovations can significantly enhance community acceptance, reduce slippage from ODF status, and foster sustainable sanitation practices in Bauchi State.

items.titel: The enhanced capabilities of mid-infrared limb emission sounding to observe stratospheric aerosol injection geoengineering
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract. Using a model-based pseudo-reality (PR) future scenario and realistic pseudo-observations (POs) representative for a proposed satellite mission concept (CAIRT – the Changing-Atmosphere Infra-Red Tomography explorer), we analyse the capabilities of a high-spectral-resolution limb-emission sounding techniques to detect and quantitatively monitor very weak stratospheric aerosol injections (SAI) geoengineering interventions, in terms of the injected sulphur dioxide (SO2) and its evolution into sulphate aerosols (SA). Our results suggest that this technique would detect SO2 injections, at the horizontal and vertical scale, within hours to a few days since the SAI deployment. This concept would quantify the SO2 injected mass, even for injections of the order of magnitude of a few to some tens of tonnes of SO2, characteristic of "near-term" to "mid-term" experiments feasible even unilaterally/illegally, or in the context of small-scale outdoor experiments, with presently existing technology and at relatively low cost. In addition, our results suggest that this concept would be able to track the temporal evolution of the subsequently formed SA, as it spreads zonally and then toward higher latitudes through meridional dispersion, and to monitor changes in its vertical distribution over time through processes like self-lofting of the resulting SA plume. items.titel: Trade‐Offs in Sustainable Development? The Relationship Between the Sustainable Development Goals and Circular Economy Outcomes in the European Union
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Countries around the world have committed to a range of sustainable development initiatives aimed at advancing the Sustainable Development Goals and promoting the circular economy. However, the implementation of these sustainability initiatives entails substantial costs and resource requirements which may result in potential trade‐offs. We examine these sustainability trade‐offs by focusing on the relationship between the Sustainable Development Goals and the circular economy. Drawing on a panel dataset of European Union member states spanning 2009–2021, we find that progress on the Sustainable Development Goals is negatively associated with circular economy outcomes, indicating potential trade‐offs between these major sustainability initiatives. Furthermore, we find that strong environmental policy settings within ruling governments, higher levels of government spending, and greater trade freedom positively moderate the relationship between the Sustainable Development Goals and circular economy outcomes, thereby reducing sustainability trade‐offs. The findings of this study contribute to extant theory and have implications for policymakers.

items.titel: Developing a resource-based analysis of technological innovation systems: The case of digital innovation in Dutch processing industries
items.samenvatting_bron: Resource-based perspectives in Technological Innovation Systems (TIS) research offer new insights into innovation dynamics and address gaps in the traditional structure-function approach. We take stock of this perspective to develop a framework that enhances TIS in two ways. First, we improve the conceptual linkage between TIS elements and functions by focusing on innovation resources and their dynamics. Next, we offer a combined view of system-building and hindering processes by identifying and characterizing meso-level TIS mechanisms through micro-level resource changes. We apply our framework to a qualitative case study on the digital TIS within the Dutch processing industry. The analysis generalizes four system-building activities and four systemic problems, which emerge from the presence, accessibility, applicability, and scale of innovation resources. Additionally, four case-specific mechanisms are identified which illustrate tensions between positive and negative dynamics, revealing fundamental complexity underlying the overall TIS functioning. Our framework provides a basis for unpacking such tensions and identifying more targeted policy interventions, particularly for innovation systems of general-purpose technologies.

items.titel: Changes in travel time ratios (TTR) before and during the first COVID-19 lockdown in Austria
items.samenvatting_bron: COVID-19 has profoundly affected travel behaviour, and numerous studies have examined its impact on daily activities. However, relatively little attention has been paid to the trade-offs between activity-location choices, associated travel times, and the durations of activities undertaken at those locations. This paper addresses this gap by analysing how long individuals travel to reach different activity destinations and how much time they ultimately spend there, and how this balance varies across trip purposes, journey structures, and socio-demographic groups before and during the COVID-19 lockdown. The analysis draws on two waves of a seven-day travel and time-use diary survey conducted in Austria. Consistent with previous research, the results confirm that both the number of journeys and the frequency of out-of-home activities declined sharply during the lockdown. However, changes in the trade-off between travel time and activity duration were heterogeneous across activity purposes, journey types, and socio-demographic groups. In particular, work-related activities generally exhibited declining Travel Time Ratio (TTR) values, while several discretionary activities showed increases. These differentiated shifts reflect systematic differences in socio-demographic characteristics, activity structures, and journey configurations, indicating that individuals adjusted unevenly to altered capability, authority, and coupling constraints. items.titel: Culture Wars: Subcreation and the Narrative Contestation of Cultivated Meat
items.samenvatting_bron: Cultivated meat – meat grown from animal cells in bioreactors – has become a symbolic flashpoint in contemporary culture wars, framed not as a technical innovation but as either moral salvation or civilizational threat. We argue that these conflicts arise through temporalized narrative subcreation: the construction of emotionally charged storyworlds that embed cultural values within divergent orientations toward past and future, continuity and change. Analyzing proponent and opponent discourse, we show how both sides mobilize the same core values – tradition, identity, and autonomy – yet transform them into polarized narratives by projecting them into distinct temporal storyworld genres. Our framework theorizes culture wars as contests of temporal meaning-making, where legitimacy hinges on competing subcreated worlds that render innovations morally legible. By revealing the temporal and narrative structures underpinning these conflicts, we offer a portable analytic lens for understanding legitimacy struggles surrounding other disruptive innovations, including climate action, reproductive technologies, and AI governance.

items.titel: Institutional risk, finance, and the limits of techno-economic optimality in green hydrogen deployment
items.samenvatting_bron: Green hydrogen is widely positioned as a key option for deep decarbonization, yet large-scale deployment remains limited despite growing techno-economic potential. This review examines how non-technical conditions influence the feasibility of green hydrogen business models, using the Netherlands as an illustrative case. A review-driven mixed-methods framework integrates evidence from a systematic literature review, semi-structured expert interviews, and an established hourly-resolved techno-economic optimization model to examine how policy design, investment risk, infrastructure constraints, and demand formation influence both the levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) and deployment feasibility. A multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) is employed to synthesize qualitative and quantitative evidence and prioritize the principal drivers and barriers identified across the different sources. The synthesized evidence, supported by the illustrative techno-economic analysis, indicates that LCOH values below €6 kg −1 are attainable under favorable assumptions, including low renewable electricity prices, reduced weighted average cost of capital (WACC), and access to underground hydrogen storage. However, regulatory fragmentation, grid congestion, weak demand coordination, and limited institutional legitimacy substantially constrain the realization of such conditions in practice. items.titel: The four ways of knowing: revising the 4P model of knowing through a non-dual and reflexive perspective
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Vervaeke and Mastropietro’s 4P model of knowing is a non-representational and process-oriented framework that integrates four interrelated ways of knowing: propositional, procedural, perspectival, and participatory. In this paper, we revise this model, drawing on the enactive approach and insights from Madhyamaka and Yogācāra Buddhist traditions of philosophy. We first provide an integrated overview of the 4P model and identify three questions concerning the conceptualization of participatory knowing and the ontological status of distinctions between the four ways of knowing. We then introduce the enactive and Buddhist resources that inform our treatment, and address these questions through a non-dual and reflexive treatment that preserves the framework’s pedagogical and transformative potential. Finally, we discuss how the revised framework can inform fields as diverse as education, psychotherapy, and contemplative pedagogy.

items.titel: Double energy vulnerability in Eastern Europe: quantifying and verifying regional sensitivity to the phenomenon
items.samenvatting_bron: This study considers 57 regions from 8 Eastern European countries and quantifies the sensitivity to double energy vulnerability of each region by developing a composite indicator. Double energy vulnerability is a concept describing simultaneous exposure to energy and transport poverty. Eastern European countries present high levels of double energy vulnerability; nonetheless, remaining an understudied macro-region. To understand the dependency between double energy vulnerability and rurality and tenure, the results are then compared with the rurality levels of the different regions, and to the national proportion spent on energy and transport services. The developed indicator provides an analysis of the phenomenon across Eastern Europe, quantifying regions' sensitivity to it by combining indicators stemming from different dimensions. Data from 2015 to 2024 was considered. Bulgaria is found to be the country presenting the highest level of double energy vulnerability. For the latter specifically, data at higher spatial resolution was utilised to have a more detailed understanding and to assess the obtained results. Finally, the results were verified by performing interviews with relevant experts in the field, considering also non-quantifiable aspects. The results provide a clearer picture of Eastern European regions' sensitivity to double energy vulnerability, highlighting the most sensitive ones.

items.titel: Interdisciplinary Research on Real Estate
items.samenvatting_bron: The proceedings of the Conference of Interdisciplinary Research on Real Estate (CIRRE) from 2016–2025 demonstrate the evolution of real estate research into an interdisciplinary, human-centred, and systems-oriented field that addresses complex societal, environmental, and technological challenges. A key lesson is the importance of integrating perspectives from law, economics, architecture, engineering, sociology, psychology, and environmental sciences. This interdisciplinary approach enables more comprehensive solutions to issues such as housing inequality, urban resilience, and sustainable development. Human well-being has remained a central focus throughout the decade. Research increasingly emphasizes residential satisfaction, participatory planning, accessibility, and the needs of aging populations, culminating in studies on aging in place and smart home technologies. This reinforces the principle that successful real estate solutions should prioritize users’ quality of life alongside technical and economic objectives. Sustainability has evolved from a conceptual aspiration into a practical imperative. CIRRE research highlights low-carbon development, circular economy principles, energy-efficient renovations, and resilience to climate change and global crises, emphasizing the integration of environmental, social, and economic sustainability. items.titel: Switching Patterns of Oral Retinoids to Alternative Medications: An Interrupted Time-Series Analysis of Four European Countries
items.samenvatting_bron: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The European Pregnancy Prevention Program for oral retinoids was updated in 2018, yet its impact on switching to retinoid alternative medications remains unclear. Thus, we aimed to measure its impact on the switching patterns from oral retinoids to retinoid alternative medications in women of childbearing potential in four European countries. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in six databases across four European countries: the Netherlands (NL-PHARMO), Spain (ES-VID and ES-BIFAP), Italy (IT-ARS and IT-Caserta) and Denmark (DK-DNR), covering women of childbearing potential prescribed/dispensed oral retinoid between 2010 and 2020. The utilisation of retinoid alternative medications and switching from oral retinoids to retinoid alternative medications after discontinuation were measured. Changes in the rates of switching before and after implementation of the Pregnancy Prevention Program were analysed using an interrupted time series analysis. RESULTS: From 88,992 women of childbearing potential previously exposed to retinoids, 32.0% (28,446) switched to a retinoid alternative medication over the study period. Overall, ten out of 80 median discontinuers per month switched. Median switching monthly rates ranged from 1.8 to 6.5% and from 1.2 to 2.3% pre-implementation and post-implementation, respectively. items.titel: REScoops acting as intermediaries, influencing the scaling of energy communities; a multi-case analysis of five pilots in Europe
items.samenvatting_bron: There is increasing scholarly attention to the scaling of energy communities (EC). Intermediaries have an important role here. Energy communities themselves, especially in the form of renewable energy cooperatives (REScoops), can take on this role very well. This paper addresses the question how REScoops, acting as intermediaries, influence the scaling of ECs. A longitudinal multi-case research design is adopted to answer this question. Five cases of EC pilots in different EU countries receiving intermediary support from REScoops were selected and researched over a three-year period. Data collection involved interviews, text documents, a quantitative longitudinal survey, and pilot project data. Results show that EC organisations use various forms of scaling: scaling-up, -out, and -deep. Regarding REScoops acting as an intermediary influencing the scaling of ECs, the analysis presents moderate support for positive impact. The relationship appears positive for scaling-deep and fairly positive for scaling-out. For scaling-up the relationship there was mostly within-case evidence. Scaling-up appears related to contextual factors. A fairly challenging context seems correlated to ECs deploying scaling-up strategies, using REScoop intermediary agency with the aim of changing key institutional structures, regulatory and policy frameworks that have a negative impact on ECs. This paper ends with suggestions for future work.

items.titel: Bony labyrinth taxonomic identification and long-term evolution of livestock in the Southwest and Central Asia
items.samenvatting_bron: Southwest and Central Asia were pivotal regions for the domestication and dispersal of domestic herbivores. Here we investigate long-term variation in bony labyrinth morphology of domestic bovids (sheep, goats and cattle) across the last 10 000 years. We focused on the osseous cavity of the inner ear, located within the petrous bone. We analysed semicircular canal (SC) size and shape using micro-computed tomography and geometric morphometrics (GMM) on 78 modern reference specimens and 234 archaeological petrous bones from 51 sites spanning the Iranian Plateau, Central Asia, the Caucasus and the Indus Valley. Bony labyrinth morphometrics yielded a strong taxonomic signal, enabling species-level identification of 228 out of 234 specimens and revealing greater diversity than anticipated. Comparative analyses further documented contrasting, nonlinear diachronic trajectories in SC size and shape among sheep, goats and cattle, reflecting species-specific responses to domestication and long-term herd management. Together, these results demonstrate that bony labyrinth GMM provides a robust, non-destructive framework for taxonomic identification and evolutionary inference and underscore how long-term, interdisciplinary approaches can capture the complex, nonlinear dynamics of animal domestication across the longue durée.

items.titel: Poisoned arrows in the Danish Early Mesolithic: Testing lithic ballistic morphometrics against faunal and archaeobotanical data
items.samenvatting_bron: Throughout human deep history, lithic tool components became periodically very small. Such microlithic tools are the signature artefacts of the European Mesolithic in general, and the iconic Danish Mesolithic in particular. Sandwiched between the end of the Pleistocene and the emergence of agricultural lifeways, the Danish Mesolithic is characterised by marked changes in microlith design from lanceolates to geometrics and finally to transversal forms with wide front edges. These changes are synonymous with the transitions between the traditionally defined cultures of the Early, Middle and Late Mesolithic, yet the forces shaping them remain opaque. Here we present lithic, faunal, and a combination of archaeobotanical and palaeobotanical proxies, suggesting that the use of arrow poison was a likely driver for microlithic design change. An analysis of ballistically relevant morphometric attributes of lithics found in direct association with hunted prey suggests that the use of poison was prevalent during the Early Mesolithic when targeted game animals were also largest. Thereafter, lithic projectile points became larger and game animals smaller, likely reflecting Holocene faunal downsizing alongside changing hunting strategies. Palaeobotanical evidence from Denmark and southern Sweden suggests that a wide range of toxic plants were available throughout the Holocene. items.titel: A Call for Systematic Integration of Family‐Focused Care in Clinical Nursing Practice in Europe: A Position Paper
items.samenvatting_bron: AIM: To highlight the need for a shift to family-focused care and to outline how this transition should be developed and implemented through close collaboration between clinical practice and research. DESIGN: Position paper. METHOD: Members of Family Health in Europe-Research in Nursing (FAME-RN) developed the position paper through an iterative process informed by selected literature, established care models and collective expertise in family nursing. The paper examines distinctions between patient-centred, person-centred, family-centred and family-focused care and considers key barriers, enablers and priorities for implementation across European healthcare settings. RESULTS: Family-focused care recognises families as essential partners in caring for individuals with severe or chronic conditions across the lifespan, working with families as interconnected systems and as an explicit unit of nursing assessment and intervention rather than solely involving them as individuals in care. The position paper identifies key priorities for implementation including conceptual clarity, systematic family assessment, family-level interventions, education and competence development, organisational leadership, supportive policy, co-design with families and implementation-focused research. CONCLUSION: Ensuring that families have access to appropriate information, support and resources enhances caregiving capacity while protecting family health and well-being. items.titel: Strategising social innovation paradoxes: four faces of energy citizenship
items.samenvatting_bron: Social innovation (SI) is an increasingly prominent area of innovation. Involving changes in social relations, SI practice is pervaded with tensions and apparent paradoxes, however. The ‘productive use of paradox’ has been articulated theoretically and demonstrated empirically, but much remains to be elaborated in terms of SI strategies. This contribution explores the SI paradoxes from a paradox management angle. Striving for conceptual insight with empirical concreteness, the analysis invokes the example of energy citizenship. Defined as a shift from passive consumerism towards active political engagement with energy systems, it harbours several tensions. Building on empirical investigations in Belgium, we discuss and strategise four contrasting manifestations of energy citizenship. This empirical diversity helps to showcase paradoxes pertaining to citizenship, intermediation, institutionalisation and materiality. The analysis combines insights from social innovation scholarship, critical innovation studies and governance research to situate these paradoxes in wider SI discussions. Comparing paradox-handling strategies within and across energy citizenship examples, we unpack and nuance the idea of paradoxes as the ‘working substance’ of social innovation. items.titel: Opnieuw eenrichtingsverkeer voor scheepvaart op IJssel door lage waterstand
items.samenvatting_bron: De scheepvaart op de IJssel tussen de IJsselkop en Zutphen mag sinds vanochtend opnieuw maar in één richting varen. Rijkswaterstaat heeft de maatregel opnieuw ingesteld vanwege de lage waterstand. Schepen moeten daardoor weer zo'n 300 kilometer omvaren. Maandag werd het eenrichtingsverkeer nog opgeheven , omdat de minimaal gepeilde diepte op de Boven-IJssel de vereiste 1,45 meter had bereikt. Doordat er minder regen is gevallen dan verwacht, is de waterstand weer onder die grens gedaald, meldt Rijkswaterstaat. De binnenvaart mag nu alleen stroomopwaarts varen. Schepen die vanuit Duitsland de IJssel op willen, kunnen daardoor niet bij Arnhem richting Zutphen varen. Ze moeten omvaren via Amsterdam en het IJsselmeer. Het eenrichtingsverkeer heeft ook gevolgen voor de binnenvaart richting het Twentekanaal, schrijft RTV Oost . Schippers kunnen niet meer vanuit beide richtingen rechtstreeks naar het kanaal varen en moeten dus omvaren. Waterstand blijft dalen Rijkswaterstaat verwacht dat de waterstand de komende vijf dagen verder daalt. Dat hangt onder meer af van de hoeveelheid water die via de Rijn bij Lobith Nederland binnenkomt. Regen in Duitsland en Zwitserland kan ervoor zorgen dat de waterstanden weer stijgen. De waterstanden worden daarom nauwlettend in de gaten gehouden. Als die veranderen, kunnen ook de maatregelen voor de scheepvaart worden aangepast.

items.titel: Machine learning-based prediction of critical load events in airborne wind energy systems
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract. Predicting and avoiding critical load events is crucial for the reliable autonomous operation of airborne wind energy (AWE) systems. Such events can lead to actuator saturation, loss of steering authority, and increased structural stresses, eventually resulting in long-term degradation of the kite, tether, and ground-station components. The present study explores a data-driven approach to predicting tether force peaks, defined as instances in which the force exceeds a threshold set by the winch controller. The method is developed using a large-scale SCADA dataset from Kitepower's leading-edge inflatable V9 kite, including more than 1000 pumping cycles spanning 26 h of kite operation and covering a wide range of wind and operating conditions. Tether force peaks are detected and used to extract pre-peak time windows that capture the system behavior before each threshold exceedance. From these windows, statistical, temporal, and spectral features are computed from multiple kite, tether, and ground-station measurements. A supervised classification model is trained to distinguish normal operation from pre-peak dynamics. The proposed approach predicts critical load events 1 s in advance and shows strong generalization capability on flight data that was not used for training the model, correctly identifying 85.4 % of the critical load events (recall) and achieving a 90.9 % F1-score, a metric that indicates a strong balance between correctly detected events and false alarms

items.titel: From fragmented knowledge to scalable wetland restoration in Europe: The Restore4Life Integrated Wetland Reconstruction Accelerator
items.samenvatting_bron: Europe’s commitment to restore degraded ecosystems has created an urgent need to move from isolated restoration projects towards approaches that can be replicated and scaled. Wetland restoration, however, remains constrained by fragmented knowledge, incompatible datasets, inconsistent monitoring, limited transfer of experience between sites, weak stakeholder participation and insufficient links between ecological planning and long-term financing. Restore4Life addresses these barriers through an Integrated Wetland Reconstruction Accelerator that connects scientific evidence, digital decision support, field implementation, participation and finance throughout the restoration cycle. Within this framework, reconstruction refers to the active re-establishment of wetland structures, processes and functions where passive recovery alone is insufficient. The Accelerator provides a common operational framework for identifying restoration opportunities, establishing ecological baselines, selecting indicators, designing interventions, monitoring outcomes and comparing restoration trajectories. These approaches are being tested across contrasting freshwater, floodplain, deltaic and coastal demonstration sites and translated into harmonised protocols, transferable solutions and practical implementation roadmaps. items.titel: Employing environmental DNA to evaluate invasive species removal and spatiotemporal dynamics of pupfish, crayfish, and Green Sunfish in a desert spring system
items.samenvatting_bron: Aquatic invasive species disrupt ecosystem function and threaten native biodiversity through predation, competition, and habitat alteration. Eradication offers the best chance for ecosystem recovery but requires substantial time and resources, and detection of invasives at low densities is challenging. Environmental DNA (eDNA) sampling of genetic material shed by organisms into the environment provides a sensitive, cost-effective, and noninvasive alternative to traditional detection methods. In this study, we applied eDNA methods to inform invasive species eradication at Ash Meadows National Wildlife Refuge and explore spatiotemporal dynamics of endangered Ash Meadows Amargosa Pupfish (Cyprinodon nevadensis mionectes), and invasive Green Sunfish (Lepomis cyanellus), and Red Swamp Crayfish (Procambarus clarkii) in the target warm spring system. First, we quantified eDNA transport using a caged Green Sunfish experiment, then used these results to inform repeated eDNA sampling alongside traditional capture methods (gill nets, trap nets, electrofishing) to determine Green Sunfish distribution, target removal efforts, and evaluate eradication. Modeling indicated that collection of one sample every 160 m yielded >0.95 detection probability for 3 fish, while collection of 10 samples was required to reach the same detection probability for 1 fish (95% CI: 2–57). items.titel: Onderzoek naar een nieuwe, op DNA gebaseerde selectiemethode voor het identificeren van genclusters voor de biosynthese van antibiotica
items.samenvatting_bron: Antibiotics are indispensable for modern medicine as they allow the treatment of infectious diseases and enable invasive medical procedures. However, their incorrect and widespread use has caused an increase in antibiotic resistance, making the discovery of novel antibiotics urgent. Most antibiotics in clinical use are derived from micro-organisms. Unfortunately, traditional techniques suffer from the limited culturability and sensitivity needed to detect antibiotic-producing organisms, resulting in the discovery of only the "low hanging fruit" of antibiotic candidates. Accessing the large potential known to be still present in nature therefore requires new approaches to circumvent these limitations and expand the repertoire of antibiotics known today. In this work, we aimed to set the first steps towards a novel approach, using a polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based droplet-platform to adopt a genotype-based, culture-independent method with increased throughput and sensitivity. A PCR-assay with newly developed degenerate primers will be used to enrich gene cluster types of interest. Combined with high-throughput screening of large metagenomic libraries, built with environmental DNA (eDNA), and functional characterization of recovered clones, we anticipate that this approach will enable the detection of a larger diversity of antibiotics and complement current detection methodologies.

items.titel: Coastal benthic ecosystems in a changing ocean: a mini review
items.samenvatting_bron: Coastal benthic ecosystems are shaped by the combined effects of climate change and anthropogenic pressures. Ocean warming, acidification, and deoxygenation interact with eutrophication, pollution, bottom trawling, and coastal development, altering biodiversity, habitat structure, and functioning from shallow coasts to continental margins. Benthic communities, comprising infaunal and epifaunal taxa, regulate key processes including nutrient cycling, sediment dynamics, and carbon burial, thereby underpinning benthic-pelagic coupling and biogeochemical dynamics. Rising temperatures and marine heatwaves drive widespread losses of habitat-forming species, while ocean acidification constrains calcification. Warming, acidification, hypoxia, eutrophication, and pollution increasingly simplify assemblages, and alter trophic pathways and performance. Interactions among stressors can amplify organismal sensitivity and push ecosystems towards ecological thresholds. However, many knowledge gaps remain. Recent methodological advances, including environmental DNA metabarcoding, automated imaging, trait-based analyses, and multi-stressor experiments, are improving the detection of ecosystem changes at large and our mechanistic understanding of ecosystem responses to ongoing change. items.titel: Simple soil eDNA sampling reveals terrestrial mammal diversity in the Central Kalahari and highlights waterholes as sampling hotspots
items.samenvatting_bron: Remote and vast ecosystems present a challenge for biodiversity monitoring. The Central Kalahari Game Reserve in Botswana is one such ecosystem spanning 52,800 km2, a mosaic of fossilized rivers, clay pans, semi-arid sand dunes, scrub, and woodland. It is one of the last remaining untouched wildernesses in the world and hosts unique biodiversity, including populations of threatened mammals. Due to its extreme arid environment, size, and inaccessibility, surveying biodiversity across the reserve is both logistically and technically difficult. Here we demonstrate that a low-effort approach of sampling soil across the reserve is an efficient way to rapidly assess the terrestrial mammal biodiversity using eDNA metabarcoding. We found that eDNA from soil near waterholes performed better at capturing local biodiversity than soil from roads. eDNA metabarcoding detected 38 mammal species, 15 bird species and two amphibians and a simultaneously conducted camera trapping study detected 29 mammal species. eDNA was particularly powerful for detecting small-bodied taxa, including murids, mongooses and bats, which were largely missed by camera traps, while camera trapping was aimed at and performed well for detecting felids. Mammal species that had a higher activity nearby eDNA sampling points (i.e., a higher number of camera trapping recordings nearby) had a higher probability of being detected via eDNA. items.titel: Community-Driven Fisheries Innovations for Climate Adaptation and a Sustainable Blue Economy
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Small-scale fisheries are among the most climate-vulnerable socio-ecological systems, facing threats from rising sea temperatures, ocean acidification, extreme weather, and shifting species distributions. Yet, they are also dynamic sites of innovation where communities develop adaptive solutions. Drawing on a non-systematic review of literature from 2016–2025, this article synthesizes community-led innovations across Africa, Asia, Oceania, Europe, and Latin America and examines how local ecological knowledge, co-management, and technological practices converge to strengthen resilience. Across regions, empowerment emerges as both a mechanism and an outcome: women’s cooperatives in Nigeria and Mexico increased household security, youth-driven digital platforms in Ecuador and Hawaii built adaptive capacity, and Indigenous stewardship in North America safeguarded both biodiversity and cultural continuity. Scaling these innovations requires supportive governance, access to finance, and protections for local agencies. Far from being marginal, community-driven fisheries innovations are central to climate adaptation and must be recognized as core strategies for building a sustainable blue economy.

items.titel: Carbon Offsets 2.0
items.samenvatting_bron: Carbon offsetting was a well-intended but ill-fated model, ravaged by a lack of trust crisis stemming from methodological vices—additionality, permanence, and transparency—which has led to accusations of greenwashing and undermined the effectiveness of the entire procedure. This chapter suggests that a new paradigm, Carbon Offsets 2.0, is being formed, which is based on three non-negotiable pillars to reclaim integrity and impact. The first pillar, trust, is designed with the help of science-based standards such as the Core Carbon Principles and effective community involvement with the help of Free, Prior, and Informed Consent. The second is transparency which is a digital revolution of satellites monitoring, AI and blockchain to establish an unchangeable, open registry of all credits. The third pillar, Real Impact, will change the market dynamics associated with low-cost avoidance to high-durability carbon dioxide removal and initiatives that provide verifiable co-benefits. The chapter discusses the shifting implement tools of next-generation approaches, such as improved nature-based solutions or technological carbon removal and the new financing, including the advance market commitment, that can be used to support them.

items.titel: Traditional villages in the Nhue River Green Belt, Hanoi, Vietnam: a biophilic landscape framework for healthy and resilient urbanization
items.samenvatting_bron: Rapid urbanization and climate change are increasing pressure on traditional villages within Hanoi’s Nhue River Green Belt, where settlements, agricultural land, water systems, cultural heritage, and local livelihoods coexist within a strategic ecological buffer. While research on biophilic urbanism and healthy cities often focuses on parks, green–blue infrastructure, street greening, and building-scale design, less attention has been given to green-belt villages as socio-ecological landscape systems with potential health-supportive capacities. This paper develops a typology-based framework for ecological landscape organization supporting urban health. Drawing on policy review, field observation, spatial analysis, and secondary data, the study identifies key landscape assets and pressures, including water systems, productive and livelihood landscapes, cultural–social spaces, slow-mobility networks, and courtyard housing. Villages are differentiated by their relationship with water, spatial structure, and livelihood characteristics, and these assets are then translated into five health-related landscape capacities. The findings provide practical guidance for planning and policy by reframing green-belt villages as health-supportive ecological landscape infrastructure. The framework supports development control, landscape co-governance, everyday nature contact, cultural-place identity, and climate-adaptive public space, offering a transferable approach for healthier and more res

items.titel: The EU, US, and China
items.samenvatting_bron: As the climate crisis intensifies, the scientific consensus is clear: reducing emissions alone is no longer sufficient. The large-scale removal of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere is now a critical pillar for achieving global net-zero targets. This chapter examines the emerging global carbon removal economy, focusing on the divergent strategies, strengths, and weaknesses of the three primary economic and geopolitical actors: the European Union, the United States, and China. Moving beyond a simple technological comparison, it analyzes the interplay of policy, innovation, investment, and underlying philosophy that is shaping this nascent but vital industry. The chapter argues that while the US currently leads in market-creation and high-risk innovation, the EU excels in regulatory frameworks and methodological rigor, and China holds unparalleled potential for rapid deployment of nature-based solutions and industrial scale-up. The ultimate "leader" is not yet decided, and the evolving dynamics between these powers will fundamentally shape the cost, efficacy, and governance of carbon removal for decades to come.

items.titel: Biochar in Stabilizing Soil Organic Carbon and Building a Sustainable Bioeconomy
items.samenvatting_bron: Biochar appears to be a natural remedy that can enhance the stabilization of soil organic carbon (SOC). Biochar effectively enhances SOC stabilization and is increasingly recognized as a nature-based solution for developing sustainable bioeconomy pathways. This chapter discuss the soils in terms of their capacity to stabilize and store organic carbon. Soils serve as the ultimate carbon sink in terrestrial ecosystems. A high risk of SOC depletion has been reported in South Asian agroecosystems due to their intensive land use change, poor residue management, and climate-related stressors. According to recent studies, biochar has significant potential to replace depleted SOC with stable black carbon. The chapter also discusses the stabilization of SOC, its density and threat to degrade. This chapter provide essential insights for understanding the nature and dynamics of SOC pathways and mechanisms under dynamic soil conditions. The chapter also discusses important and critical aspects of biochar and black carbon along with their use in Indigenous soils, known as Terra preta.

items.titel: Reproducibility package for "Climate Adaptive Capacity, Health-System Resilience, and Tuberculosis Mortality in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Longitudinal Two-Way Fixed-Effects Panel Analysis, 2010–2023"
items.samenvatting_bron: This record contains the reproducibility package for the study “Climate Adaptive Capacity, Health-System Resilience, and Tuberculosis Mortality in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Longitudinal Two-Way Fixed-Effects Panel Analysis, 2010–2023”. The package includes derived analytic files, data dictionaries, source-data manifest, reproducibility scripts, direction and estimability audit outputs for ND-GAIN climate indicators, adjustment-set sensitivity analyses, two-way fixed-effects model outputs, robustness analyses, programme-plausibility check outputs, and manuscript-supporting materials. Input data sources are publicly available from the WHO Global TB Programme, ND-GAIN Country Index, and World Bank. The uploaded files are intended to support transparency and reproducibility of the ecological country-level panel analysis. Raw third-party source datasets are not redistributed beyond derived analytic and documentation files where permitted. The study received an exemption determination from the Khon Kaen University Ethics Committee for Human Research, project number HE691462.

items.titel: Implementation of agricultural nutrient mitigation policies and nature-based solutions in Baltic and North Sea countries
items.samenvatting_bron: Nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) emissions from agricultural lands contribute to eutrophication and the degradation of surface waters. This paper studies the implementation of European agri-environmental policies to regulate these emissions in the North European coastal waters by promoting changes in agricultural practices through nutrient mitigation measures and nature-based solutions (NbS). By analyzing policy documents and results from co-creation, it compares the implementation of agricultural nutrient mitigation policies in four Baltic Sea countries—Denmark, Sweden, Finland, and Poland—as well as Norway, which borders the Atlantic and the North Sea. The findings suggest that water quality should be set as a priority in national implementation. Integrating NbS, ensuring stability and aligning agricultural practices with environmental goals would reduce the risk of eutrophication in marine ecosystems.

items.titel: IFAD Impact Assessment - Nepal (Federal Democratic Republic of) Adaptation for Smallholders in Hilly Areas Project (ASHA)
items.samenvatting_bron: The Adaptation for Smallholders in Hilly Areas Project (ASHA) was designed to enhance climate resilience among vulnerable smallholder farmers through a combination of grants, training, and capacity-building initiatives. Central to its approach was the strengthening of local climate adaptation planning via Local Adaptation Plans of Action (LAPAs) and the promotion of climate-smart agriculture through farmer field schools. The project also supported the development of climate-resilient communal infrastructure and encouraged climate-adaptive, income-generating activities, such as vegetable cultivation, agroforestry and livestock management, leveraging both financial and in-kind contributions from participating communities. This impact assessment of ASHA was conducted in 2023 using a mixed-methods approach that combines quantitative household and community-level surveys with qualitative interviews.

items.titel: Beyond Green Materials
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Climate adaptation governance in Pacific Small Island Developing States is increasingly influenced by market-oriented frameworks, including climate finance, private-sector partnerships, and resilience investment initiatives. While these approaches have expanded adaptation finance, they have also narrowed how resilience is understood and governed. They marginalize Indigenous systems of stewardship, customary governance, and community-led adaptation. This article examines bamboo-based adaptation in the district of Tai Vugalei, Fiji. It reframes bamboo not as a nature-based solution or green material but as Indigenous adaptive infrastructure rooted in custodianship, reciprocity, and community governance. Drawing on talanoa, a Pacific Indigenous approach to dialogue, storytelling, and knowledge sharing, alongside participant observation and lived Indigenous participation, the article shows how bamboo supports durable livelihoods and reparable infrastructure through communal learning, local governance, and practices that have endured over generations. The findings demonstrate how growing efforts to commercialize, standardize, and scale bamboo—how it is institutionalized, commercialized, and governed as it moves beyond village contexts—create tensions between community-based governance and market-oriented development pathways. items.titel: When does urban greening jointly mitigate urban heat and air pollution? A systematic evidence map of co-benefits, trade-offs and failure conditions
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban heat and air pollution are two major environmental challenges affecting urban sustainability, public health and quality of life. Urban green spaces, including parks, urban forests, street trees and other ground-level vegetation, are widely promoted as nature-based solutions to address these challenges. However, although vegetation can reduce temperatures through shading and evapotranspiration, its effects on air pollution are more complex. Dense vegetation may restrict airflow and pollutant dispersion, while some plant species release biogenic volatile organic compounds that contribute to atmospheric pollution. Consequently, improvements in thermal conditions do not necessarily lead to improvements in air quality. The primary purpose of this research is to systematically examine when and under what conditions urban greening provides simultaneous benefits for urban heat mitigation and air pollution reduction, when trade-offs occur, and which environmental and spatial factors influence these outcomes. The review also investigates whether improvements in environmental conditions translate into measurable reductions in human exposure or improvements in health and wellbeing. The research addresses five key questions: Under what conditions does urban greening improve both thermal conditions and air quality? items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Introduction Biocrusts, complex communities of microorganisms closely associated with soil, are essential components of drylands, supporting soil stability, water availability, and nutrient cycling. Inoculation with biocrust‐forming cyanobacteria has emerged as a promising nature‐based solution to restore degraded drylands, but large‐scale application is often constrained by challenges in production, storage, transport, and soil establishment. Objectives To address these limitations, this study explored the innovative approach of pelletizing biocrust‐forming cyanobacteria with organic amendments (paper residues, biochar, and vermicompost) to enhance inoculum delivery and performance in drylands. Methods Pellets were evaluated for physical stability, cyanobacterial viability during storage, and capacity to facilitate inoculum transfer and colonization of degraded soils. Results Paper‐based amendments showed the greatest structural integrity across the three aggregate‐stability assays, with stable fractions approximately nine‐fold higher than in unamended pellets. These formulations created a favorable microenvironment that led to increases in chlorophyll a of up to 89.4 ± 2.7% during mid‐term storage, but did not result in effective soil colonization. Tot slot gaat u in op leren, evalueren en monitoren. • Ook licht u de aanpak toe langs drie lijnen: 1. Investeren in gemeenschappen via één landelijke regeling; 2. document.tekst_begin: Ministerie van Financiën TER BESLISSING Aan de staatssecretaris van Financiën Nl ota Toezegging MP aan lid Eerdmans (JA21) over overzicht vliegbelastingen Europa Aanleiding Tijdens de Algemene Politieke Beschouwingen (APB) is door de MP naar aanleiding van een motie van het lid Eerdmans (JA21) toegezegd een overzicht van de vliegbelastingen in Europa aan de Kamer te sturen. Met deze brief komt u, mede namens de minister van IenW, tegemoet aan de toezegging van de MP. De brief is ambtelijk afgestemd met IenW en wordt parallel voorgelegd aan de minister van IenW. Beslispunten Gaat u akkoord met de verzending van de brief (bijlage 1), mede namens de minister van IenW? Zo ja, vragen wij u de Kamerbrief te ondertekenen. Gaat u akkoord met het openbaar maken van de voorliggende nota, conform de beleidslijn Actieve openbaarmaking nota's? Omlijnde delen worden voorafgaand aan openbaarmaking onzichtbaar gemaakt. items.titel: EVALUATING THE ROLE OF URBAN DESIGN TOOLS IN ENHANCING ENERGY EFFICIENCY IN HIGH-DENSITY URBAN DEVELOPMENTS: INSIGHTS FROM LAGOS METROPOLIS
items.samenvatting_bron: Urbanisation in Lagos Metropolis has increased the rate of creating high-density urban centres, thus aggravating energy demands and environmental pressures. It is in this paper that we have evaluated how urban design tools can help to reduce energy use in high-density developments in Lagos. With the Compact City Theory, Sustainable Urban Development Theory, Urban Metabolism Theory and Climate-Responsive Urban Design Theory, we used a descriptive and analytic design and preferred quantitative approaches in a mixed-method approach. The data were collected in the form of structured questionnaires filled by 384 participants, with the supplement of the information by the direct observation and GIS-based spatial analysis of the three purposely chosen high-density districts, Victoria Island, Ikeja GRA, and Surulere. The results demonstrate that mixed-use development, compact-city ideologies, passive design approaches, the street orientation, and green infrastructure have a positive effect on energy efficiency. Victoria Island was a study that proved to be a model region that has been able to adopt design tools more than Surulere and Ikeja GRA, especially using green infrastructure and orientational planning. The results of statistical analyses showed strong, positive correlations between the urban design features and the lower energy consumption, which were supported by the results of spatial overlays, which display favourable morphological patterns. items.titel: Interdisciplinary Pathways to Sustainable Finance 2.0: FinTech, Inclusion, and Decision-making Under Uncertainty
items.samenvatting_bron: Purpose: This chapter argues that the transition to Sustainable Finance 2.0 cannot be achieved through sectoral or purely technical solutions alone. Instead, it requires an interdisciplinary approach that integrates finance, digital technologies, sustainability science, and insights into human decision-making under risk and uncertainty. Need for the study: Despite rapid growth in sustainable finance and financial technology, many initiatives fail to deliver inclusive and lasting outcomes. A key reason is the insufficient consideration of behavioural, institutional, and systemic factors influencing decisions made by households, firms, and policymakers. As a result, digital financial tools may not only fall short of their goals but can also unintentionally deepen inequalities or introduce new systemic risks. Methodology: The study adopts a conceptual and analytical methodology, combining interdisciplinary literature review with qualitative comparative analysis of real-world cases. These include applications in sustainable urban development, renewable energy systems, water management, and green infrastructure. The analysis identifies patterns of effective knowledge integration as well as recurring implementation barriers. items.titel: Electrocution events of Mico rondoni (Primates: Cebidae) in the city of Porto Velho, Rondônia, Brazil
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Urbanization and habitat fragmentation expose arboreal wildlife to electrical infrastructure in Porto Velho, Rondônia state, Brazil. This study describes four fatal electrocution events involving Mico rondoni and examines the circumstances associated with the accidents. During seven months of monitoring in the Floresta neighborhood, all four deaths involved adults from the same group and occurred at a single recurrent site. The animals showed burns on the hands and feet, and one sustained trauma after falling. The concentration of events at one power-line location identifies a local electrocution hotspot but does not establish the frequency or population-level importance of this threat across the species’ range. The cases support site-specific mitigation, including technical assessment and insulation of hazardous electrical components, combined with monitored canopy crossings. Broader surveillance is required before the relevance of electrocution to M. rondoni conservation can be determined.

items.titel: The short-beaked echidna in South-East Queensland: regional data gaps and conservation risks
items.samenvatting_bron: The short-beaked echidna (Tachyglossus aculeatus) is widely distributed across Australia and is often described as common, yet robust information on abundance, demography and population trends remains sparse across much of its mainland range. This evidence gap is particularly important in South-East Queensland (SEQ), where rapid urban expansion, habitat fragmentation, dense road networks, climatic warming and the spread of the red imported fire ant (Solenopsis invicta, RIFA) may interact with the species’ slow-breeding life history. Together, these pressures could affect regional population status, while current datasets provide limited capacity to detect change. This review synthesises current knowledge relevant to echidna vulnerability and detectability and evaluates the evidence base available for SEQ, drawing on citizen science observations, wildlife hospital records and the limited peer-reviewed field studies from the region. The Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act (EPBC) listing of the Kangaroo Island echidna (T. a. multiaculeatus) is used as a cautionary case study, illustrating how chronic mortality pressures and life-history constraints can generate conservation risk that remains undetected without structured monitoring. document.tekst_begin: Vervoerplan 2027 Wagenborg Passagiersdiensten Inleiding Voor u ligt het Vervoerplan 2027 van Wagenborg Passagiersdiensten, opgesteld in het kader van de Vervoersconcessie Waddenveren Oost. Ook in 2027 staat de bereikbaarheid van Ameland en Schiermonnikoog centraal in onze dienstverlening. Samen met onze medewerkers en partners werken wij dagelijks aan een veilige, betrouwbare en toekomstbestendige verbinding tussen de eilanden en de vaste wal. 2027 staat in het teken van verdere doorontwikkeling én voorbereiding op de toekomst. Tegelijk bevinden we ons in een bijzondere fase, waarin de uitkomst van de aanbesteding voor de nieuwe concessie richtinggevend is voor de keuzes die we maken. Daarom ligt de focus in 2027 vooral op continuïteit, betrouwbaarheid en het verder verbeteren van bestaande processen, terwijl we vooruitkijken naar de periode vanaf 2029. In 2026 zijn opnieuw belangrijke stappen gezet in onze dienstverlening. Zo zijn reserverings- en digitale systemen verder ontwikkeld, is de samenwerking binnen de ketenreis versterkt en heeft de inzet van de Hiddeborg gezorgd voor meer flexibiliteit en stabiliteit binnen de sneldienstvloot. document.tekst_begin: Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal 2 Vergaderjaar 2026–2027 21 501-20 Europese Raad Nr. 2464 MOTIE VAN HET LID VAN DER PLAS Voorgesteld 12 oktober 2026 De Kamer, gehoord de beraadslaging, constaterende dat er nooit een overtuigende meerderheid voor de Natuurherstelverordening heeft bestaan, omdat de beslissende Oosten- rijkse stem voor de Natuurherstelverordening werd uitgebracht tegen de wens van de eigen regering in; constaterende dat Nederland tegen de Natuurherstelverordening heeft gestemd; overwegende dat bij de uitwerking van de natuurherstelplannen de kosten voor de voorstanders concreter worden; overwegende dat een inventarisatie waar in het dictum om wordt verzocht, de uitvoering van de afspraak uit het coalitieakkoord over de Natuurherstelverordening niet opschort; verzoekt de regering tijdens de komende Europese top te inventariseren of er nog steeds een meerderheid is voor deze verordening, en de Kamer hierover te informeren, en gaat over tot de orde van de dag. Il suolo nelle politiche europee e italiane: verso una governance integrata per la salute e la rigenerazione
items.samenvatting_bron: Il suolo è presente da decenni nelle politiche dell’Unione europea, ma attraverso interventi settoriali e frammentati, legati di volta in volta alle politiche agricole, ambientali, climatiche, della biodiversità, delle acque e della pianificazione territoriale. Negli ultimi anni è emersa una nuova fase, caratterizzata dalla progressiva convergenza di queste politiche verso una governance più organica e integrata della risorsa suolo. Il Green Deal europeo, la EU Soil Strategy for 2030, la Missione “A Soil Deal for Europe”, la Direttiva (UE) 2025/2360 sul monitoraggio e la resilienza del suolo, il Regolamento sul carbon farming e la Nature Restoration Law delineano un quadro nel quale la salute del suolo diventa un obiettivo specifico di monitoraggio, valutazione, prevenzione, gestione e ripristino. La nuova Direttiva sul suolo rappresenta un passaggio particolarmente significativo, introducendo un quadro comune per il monitoraggio della salute dei suoli e richiedendo agli Stati membri di integrare sistemi informativi e reti di monitoraggio esistenti. Per l’Italia, ciò costituisce un’opportunità per costruire una vera infrastruttura nazionale della conoscenza del suolo, fondata sull’interoperabilità dei dati e sul coordinamento tra istituzioni. La sfida principale riguarda ora la governance nazionale. items.titel: Canalised Urban Waterways, Palimpsest Landscapes and Climate Adaptation: Comparison of Ecomorphological Trajectories from Isparta and Chelmsford
items.samenvatting_bron: This paper examines canalised urban waterways as active ecomorphological agents in the Anthropocene city through a comparative study of Isparta, Türkiye, and Chelmsford, United Kingdom. Focusing on Isparta’s Çayboyu canal and associated stream system, and Chelmsford’s canalised corridor shaped by the Rivers Chelmer and Can, the paper investigates how urban waterways form and modify relationships between urban morphology, spatial memory and public space. Canalised streams and rivers are reviewed as palimpsest landscapes and spatial corridors that continue to influence urban form, multispecies movement, and everyday experience in the age of climate change and redevelopment pressures. This study reviews how each waterway has been altered, marginalised, and reactivated within the evolving processes of urban development. The findings demonstrate that the integration of town centres depends not only on standard design solutions or location, but also on the ability to make ecological and everyday spatial relations visible and accessible. In this sense, ecomorphological trajectories contribute to debates in river restoration, ecological and morphological approaches and multispecies urban studies. Finally, the paper suggests that more permeable and adaptive approaches to canalised waterways could support spatial scenarios for reconnecting town centres with blue-green infrastructure under climate uncertainty.

items.titel: Land Use Land Cover Change, Carbon Storage Dynamics, and Future Urban Growth Simulation in Dhaka Metropolitan Area (1994-2044) Using CA-ANN and InVEST Models
items.samenvatting_bron: Rapid urbanization has dramatically transformed land use land cover (LULC) patterns and ecosystem services in megacities of the Global South, with major implications for carbon storage and climate regulation. This study investigates LULC dynamics, associated carbon storage changes, and future urban growth in the Dhaka Metropolitan Area from 1994 to 2044. Multi-temporal Landsat imagery was used to classify six LULC categories for 1994, 2004, 2014, 2019, and 2024. Carbon storage was quantified using the InVEST model by integrating LULC maps with literature-based carbon density values representing four carbon pools. Future LULC scenarios for 2034 and 2044 were simulated using a Cellular Automata–Artificial Neural Network (CA-ANN) model within the MOLUSCE framework, incorporating six biophysical and infrastructural driving factors. Model validation produced an overall accuracy of 70.13% with satisfactory kappa indices. Results reveal that built-up expansion occurred mainly at the expense of vegetation and water bodies, causing nearly a 40% decline in total carbon storage between 1994 and 2024, with water bodies contributing the largest share of carbon loss. Process-based analysis identified dominant transformation clusters driven by urban reclamation and hydrological loss, alongside vegetation clearance and land degradation. items.titel: Preliminary bat ectoparasite findings in Soppeng, Indonesia: implications for One Health surveillance
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Background Bats harbor diverse microorganisms, and their obligate ectoparasites may provide an underused surveillance layer at human–wildlife interfaces. This study assessed bat ectoparasite infestation in Soppeng Regency, South Sulawesi, and contextualized environmental-health vulnerability using Indonesian Health Survey (SKI) 2023 indicators. Methodology A cross-sectional ecological field and laboratory study examined ten bats from Taman Kalong, an urban bat roost in Watansoppeng, Soppeng Regency. Bats were inspected externally, and their fur and wing membranes were combed. Ectoparasites were preserved in 70% ethanol and examined stereomicroscopically. Infestation prevalence was calculated with an exact binomial 95% confidence interval, while abundance and intensity were summarized descriptively. Provincial SKI 2023 indicators were used only as contextual data. Results Ectoparasites were detected in all ten examined bats, corresponding to an observed sample proportion of 100.0% (10/10; exact 95% CI: 69.2–100.0%). Thirty-four ectoparasites were collected, with 2–6 specimens per bat and mean abundance and mean intensity of 3.4. items.titel: Mammalian–Environmental–DNA-Derived Probabilistic Modeling Reveals Re-Established Trophic and Co-Habitation Network Structure in Fire-Affected Terrestrial Communities
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate change threatens natural ecosystems with more frequent and intense extreme weather events, including forest fires. This study evaluated mammalian communities, a primary bio-indicator of forest health, in Uljin Forest, using both traditional camera traps and advanced environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding. Fire severity at the study sites was categorized based on field observations and satellite images using the differenced Normalized Burn Ratio. Water basins were installed for 7 days, after which the water was collected for eDNA extraction. A multi-primer approach using mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit 1 and 12S rRNA genes was employed. Comparative analysis of the mammalian relative abundance indicated that while camera traps remain the optimal tool for monitoring large mammals, eDNA methods were significantly more effective for quantifying small, cryptic species. Although long-term effects remain observable in the biodiversity and abundance of mammalian communities, Bayesian network analysis at the order level inferred positive ecological signals three years post-fire, with the food-web-related and cohabitation dynamics re-established. eDNA metabarcoding improved mammal detection relative to traditional methods and enabled probabilistic modelling to reveal ecological structure that would not be possible solely with biodiversity analysis. Overall, this multi-primer/multi-analysis approach highlights the potential of eDNA for ecosystem health monitoring.

items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Background Environmental DNA (eDNA) has transformed biodiversity monitoring, but its application for long-term ecological assessment remains limited by uncertainty in the temporal stability and consistency of eDNA signals, as well as by workflows that require specialized equipment and analytical support. Broader use of eDNA in community-based monitoring will depend on approaches that are both logistically practical and scientifically reliable. Here, we conducted two complementary studies of eDNA methods for coral reef monitoring in Hawaiʻi. First, we compared coral-specific genetic markers for tracking benthic community dynamics through time. Second, we compared passive eDNA samplers (PEDS) as a low-effort alternative to active filtration. This research was conducted in collaboration with local stewardship organizations on Oʻahu, Hawaiʻi, to assess how eDNA sampling could complement existing reef-monitoring activities and provide additional information relevant to conservation planning. items.titel: Species ecology, behavior, and substrate type shape eDNA detection of mammals at savanna waterholes
items.samenvatting_bron: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor terrestrial mammal biodiversity, yet factors that influence detection probability in such systems remain poorly understood. Substrates in and around freshwater drinking areas represent particularly promising eDNA sampling points to capture terrestrial biodiversity, especially in arid and semi-arid landscapes. However, eDNA detection probabilities are expected to depend strongly on the frequency and intensity of animal interaction with the sampled substrate at these watering holes. We combined camera trapping with eDNA metabarcoding to investigate drivers of mammal eDNA detection at savanna waterholes in South Africa (Botsalano Game Reserve) over several weeks during both wet and dry seasons and evaluated the effects of species behavior (interaction intensity with water), species traits, environmental covariates and substrate type (water versus sediment) on eDNA detection probabilities. Camera trapping detected 30 mammal species, whereas eDNA metabarcoding detected 40 species, with 25 species being shared between methods. items.titel: Community assembly dynamics in a regulated stream: Insights from environmental DNA
items.samenvatting_bron: Degradation of freshwater habitats, including the alteration of natural flow regimes by impoundment, is a major threat to native fishes. When dam removal is not possible, management actions to recover natural flow regimes can benefit native species, but monitoring community responses is crucial to show efficacy. We used eDNA metabarcoding to quantify spatiotemporal trends in fish assemblages along the longitudinal profile of a regulated stream where a court-ratified environmental flows framework is used to benefit native fishes. At a subset of sites, we also compared eDNA results with concurrent surveys conducted using long-term standardized fisheries monitoring techniques to evaluate concordance. From 59 eDNA samples collected over approximately 2 years, we detected 26 fish taxa, including 8 native species, with 25 taxa resolving to species level using a custom reference sequence database; one taxon could not be resolved between closely related species. Fish assemblages varied predictably along the longitudinal profile of the stream and by season (fall and spring). Diversity indices were higher at downstream sites and in fall, reflecting greater richness of warm-water non-native species. Evenness was similar among sites but shifts in species ranks suggests reordering processes drive spatiotemporal variation in assembly. items.titel: A washable glue for trapping pests on sticky boards in honey bee colonies
items.samenvatting_bron: Varroa mites are major pests of honey bee colonies and contribute to colony losses. Entomopathogenic fungi are a promising tool for Varroa control, but evaluating their efficacy requires follow-up infection assays. Conventional sticky board adhesives, such as petroleum jelly or vegetable oil, can trap fallen mites but are difficult to remove before testing. We developed a water-soluble glue made from cooked corn starch and glycerin that can be easily washed away with water or ethanol. The glue is prepared by cooking starch in water until thickened and then mixing it with glycerin to achieve the desired consistency. This adhesive simplifies mite recovery from sticky boards, reducing labor during mite collection and facilitating infection assays. It may also have applications in water-soluble insect traps and environmental DNA detection.

items.titel: Mapping groundwater-dependent vegetation in temperate climates on the example of Central Germany
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Groundwater-dependent ecosystems are biodiversity hotspots that provide habitat for specialized species. The European Union (EU) Water Framework Directive (WFD) stresses the importance of identifying and protecting these ecosystems. So far, most studies focus on (semi-) arid regions, where groundwater use by ecosystems is both more prevalent and easier to detect. In this study, we adapt groundwater-dependent vegetation (GDV) mapping approaches developed for dry climates to temperate regions by replacing seasonal drought-based indicators with contrasts between dry and wet years. We implement this concept by integrating for the first time to our knowledge, ECOSTRESS evapotranspiration data with high-resolution remote sensing, regional geospatial data and botanical field observations. To test our framework, we trained and validated random forest models with eight predictor variables using 166 vegetation plots to identify GDV in Central Germany. Ground-truth GDV plots prefer cooler, wetter, nutrient-richer and more acidic to alkaline environments compared to non-GDV. The final model using a phreatophyte cover threshold of 25% representing GDV plots achieved a testing accuracy of 0.97, identifying 2067 km² of GDV. Currently, only 19% is protected under the EU WFD. The proposed mapping framework offers a solution for identifying GDV in temperate regions.
